definition_zh: 失去知觉的；昏迷的；无意识的；不知不觉的；未察觉的
definition_en: not awake and not aware, or doing something without noticing it
core_image: 灯还亮着，屋里的人却睡着了，谁进门都不知道
scene: 车祸现场，一名骑手倒在路边，脸色发白，叫他也没有回应。 The injured cyclist was unconscious when the ambulance arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 unconscious 是「失去知觉的」（第 1 个义项：昏迷不醒、无反应）；句意为救护车到时那位受伤的骑车人已经昏迷。灯亮着而人不省人事，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：失去知觉的；昏迷的
形容词：无意识的；不知不觉的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「有意识的；清醒的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「无意识地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「无意识状态」

senses.title: Not awake or responsive
senses.definition: in a state like deep sleep, with no response to people or pain
senses.definitionCN: 处于类似深睡的状态，对人与疼痛都没有反应
senses.example: He was unconscious for two days after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 跌倒后他昏迷了两天。
senses.why: Conscious comes from Latin conscire, to know together with oneself, so un- removes all inner awareness.
senses.whyCN: conscious 源自拉丁语 conscire（与自己一同知道），un- 抽走了全部内在觉知。

senses.title: Done without noticing
senses.definition: done without intending or noticing it
senses.definitionCN: 做的时候既无意，也没有察觉
senses.example: She has an unconscious habit of touching her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她有个无意识摸头发的习惯。
senses.why: When the knowing part of the mind sleeps, the body still acts, and that action is called unconscious.
senses.whyCN: 知道的那部分睡着了，身体仍在动，这种动作就叫无意识。

senses.title: Not aware of something present
senses.definition: not realizing that something is there
senses.definitionCN: 没有意识到某物的存在
senses.example: They were unconscious of the risk they ran.
senses.exampleCN: 他们没有察觉自己冒的风险。
senses.why: Awareness can be switched off by inattention as well as by injury.
senses.whyCN: 觉知既可能被伤损关掉，也可能被疏忽关掉。

senses.title: The hidden part of the mind
senses.definition: in psychology, the store of feelings and memories outside awareness
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指意识之外的感受与记忆的储藏处
senses.example: Fear of failure can live in the unconscious for years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失败的恐惧可以在潜意识里住很多年。
senses.why: Since unconscious names what awareness does not reach, it becomes a noun for the region beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 unconscious 指觉知够不到的地方，它就转作名词，指那片区域本身。

senses.title: Showing feelings one does not admit
senses.definition: revealing a feeling that the person is not admitting
senses.definitionCN: 显出当事人自己并不承认的情绪
senses.example: There was an unconscious coldness in his reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答里透着一种不自觉的冷淡。
senses.why: The face reports what the mind has not yet admitted, so the expression is unconscious in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 脸会把心里还没承认的事报出来，因此这种表情是严格意义上的「无意识」。

intro.en: The word is an English negative of a Latin verb of shared knowing.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「共同知道」动词的英语否定形式。

items.en: Scire means to know, and conscire means to know with oneself, to be aware.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscire 意为与自己一同知道，即有所觉察。

items.en: Conscius is one who knows, either as a witness or as an accomplice.
items.cn: conscius 指知情者，可以是证人，也可以是同谋。

items.en: Conscious enters English in the seventeenth century with the sense of being aware.
items.cn: conscious 在十七世纪进入英语，意为有所觉察。

items.en: Unconscious follows as its negative, used first for the absence of response.
items.cn: unconscious 作为否定随后出现，最初指失去反应。

items.en: Psychology from the nineteenth century makes the noun unconscious a technical term.
items.cn: 十九世纪起心理学把名词 unconscious 变成术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sci- root of knowing, and the near-meaning group gathers states of unawareness.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「知道」的 sci- 词根，近义组汇集无察觉的状态。

entries.definition: awake and aware
the state of being aware
the inner sense of right and wrong
in a deep, unresponsive sleep
without feeling or awareness
done without thinking
awake and aware

normalIntro.en: Scire is Latin for know, so an unconscious person has no knowing at all, or none in that moment.
normalIntro.cn: scire 是拉丁语的「知道」，unconscious 的人便一点也不知道，或那一刻不知道。

normal.en: Conscious and conscience both come from knowing, one of the world and one of right and wrong.
normal.cn: conscious 与 conscience 都出自「知道」，一个知世界，一个知善恶。

normal.en: To be knocked unconscious is to have awareness switched off by force.
normal.cn: knocked unconscious 指觉知被外力关掉。

normal.en: An unconscious habit runs while the mind is busy elsewhere.
normal.cn: unconscious habit 在心神忙于别处时照常运行。

normal.en: In psychology the unconscious is a noun, the store below awareness.
normal.cn: 心理学里 the unconscious 是名词，指意识之下的储藏。

normal.en: Unconsciously is the adverb for acts done without noticing.
normal.cn: unconsciously 是副词，指没察觉地做出。

abstract.en: See a room with the light on and the person asleep in a chair.
abstract.cn: 看见一间灯还亮着的屋子，人却在椅子上睡着。

abstract.en: Watch a hand reach for the hair without the owner looking.
abstract.cn: 看一只手在主人没留神时去摸头发。

abstract.en: Then picture a cellar under that room, full of things never brought up.
abstract.cn: 再想象屋子底下有个地窖，装满从未搬上来的东西。

examples.en: The boxer was unconscious before the count reached five.
examples.cn: 数到五之前那名拳手已经失去知觉。

examples.en: He was unconscious of how loud his voice had become.
examples.cn: 他没意识到自己的嗓门已经这么大了。

examples.en: She tidied the desk unconsciously while talking on the phone.
examples.cn: 打电话时她无意识地把桌子收拾了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺坑舍斯」——俺掉进坑里，舍了什么也没感觉，人事不省。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ conscious（拉丁语 conscire「与自己一同知道」，由 com- + scire「知道」构成）；同族有 consciousness、conscience

sensesIntro.en: Every sense removes or lowers awareness, from a body that cannot respond to a mind that does not notice.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都在撤走或降低觉知：从毫无反应的身体，到毫无察觉的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room with no one awake in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯亮着却没有清醒的人在屋内。

branches.en: The body branch: knocked out and unresponsive.
branches.cn: 身体分支：被打昏、毫无反应。

branches.en: The habit branch: actions and expressions the person does not notice.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：当事人没察觉的动作与表情。

branches.en: The perception branch: a risk or fact never registered.
branches.cn: 感知分支：从未登记进来的风险或事实。

branches.en: The psychology branch, where the word becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 心理学分支：这个词在此作名词。

branches.en: The medical sense of a patient who cannot be roused.
branches.cn: 医学义：唤不醒的病人。

intro.en: A negation prefix on a Latin word for knowing with oneself.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在拉丁语「与自己一同知道」的词上。

latinIntro.en: The sci- root of knowing also gives science, conscience, and conscious.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「知道」的 sci- 词根还生出 science、conscience、conscious。

items.exampleCN: scire 支撑着 science 与 conscience。

items.example: She was conscious of the noise.

definition_zh: 有故障的；有缺陷的；错误的
definition_en: not working properly, having a flaw, or based on a mistaken idea
core_image: 天花板上的灯一闪一闪，电工拆开开关，看见一根松动的接线
scene: 灯闪了几下就灭了，问题出在一根接错的电线上。 A faulty wire made the lights flicker.
sceneCN: 这里 faulty 是「有故障的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一根有故障的电线让灯闪烁。

senses.title: Not working properly
senses.definition: not working correctly because of a defect
senses.definitionCN: 因缺陷而无法正常运转
senses.example: The faulty printer jammed twice.
senses.exampleCN: 那台有故障的打印机卡了两次纸。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday use for machines.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述机器时最常见的日常用法。

senses.title: Having a flaw
senses.definition: having a weakness or flaw in design or structure
senses.definitionCN: 设计或结构上存在弱点或瑕疵
senses.example: The plan rested on faulty assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划建立在有缺陷的假设上。
senses.why: The sense extends from machines to ideas and designs.
senses.whyCN: 该义从机器延伸到想法与设计。

senses.title: Based on a mistake
senses.definition: based on a mistaken judgment or memory
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误判断或记忆之上
senses.example: His faulty memory confused the dates.
senses.exampleCN: 他不可靠的记忆把日期弄混了。
senses.why: Human judgment can be faulty in the same way as a device.
senses.whyCN: 人的判断也可能像设备一样出故障。

intro.en: Faulty was formed in English from fault, which came from Latin fallere through Old French.
intro.cn: faulty 由 fault 在英语中加后缀构成，而 fault 经古法语源自拉丁语 fallere。

items.en: Fallere meant to deceive or cause to fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使失败。

items.en: Faute named a mistake or lack.
items.cn: faute 表示错误或缺失。

items.en: Fault entered English as a word for a mistake.
items.cn: fault 以「错误」之义进入英语。

items.en: Faulty appeared as an adjective meaning full of faults.
items.cn: faulty 作为形容词出现，意为充满缺陷的。

items.en: The word now describes machines, arguments, and memory.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词可形容机器、论证与记忆。

note.en: Faulty is compared with similar-looking words and with words for defects.
note.cn: 把 faulty 与形近词以及表示缺陷的词作比较。

entries.definition: a mistake or defect
a natural ability or a university department
a mistaken belief or false argument
having a fault or weakness
having a mark or weakness
damaged and not working

normalIntro.en: Faulty means full of faults, whether in a machine, a plan, or a memory.
normalIntro.cn: faulty 意为带有缺陷，无论指机器、计划还是记忆。

normal.en: Faulty adds -y to fault, just like health and healthy.
normal.cn: faulty 由 fault 加 -y 构成，正如 health 变 healthy。

normal.en: Faulty wiring is a common cause of fires.
normal.cn: 有故障的线路是火灾的常见原因。

normal.en: Faulty goods can be returned to the shop.
normal.cn: 有质量问题的商品可以退回商店。

normal.en: Faulty reasoning means the logic has a flaw.
normal.cn: faulty reasoning 指逻辑存在漏洞。

normal.en: Faulty hearing is not the same as deafness.
normal.cn: 听力有缺陷与完全失聪并不相同。

abstract.en: A machine, an argument, and a memory can all break in the same way.
abstract.cn: 机器、论证与记忆都可能以相似的方式出问题。

abstract.en: Calling something faulty points to a defect, not to blame.
abstract.cn: 说某物 faulty 是在指出缺陷，而非追究责任。

abstract.en: Faultless is the opposite picture of perfect working order.
abstract.cn: faultless 呈现的是完美运转的反面图景。

examples.en: The faulty heater gave off a strange smell.
examples.cn: 有故障的取暖器散发出怪味。

examples.en: Their faulty reasoning led to a poor choice.
examples.cn: 他们错误的推理导致了糟糕的选择。

examples.en: He replaced the faulty part with a new one.
examples.cn: 他用新零件替换了有故障的零件。

dict_mnemonic.text: faulty 由 fault（失误、缺陷）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，表示「带有缺陷的」。

root: 由 fault 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；fault 源自拉丁语 fallere（失误），核心义「带着缺陷的」。

sensesIntro.en: Faulty means not working properly, having a flaw, or based on a mistaken idea.
sensesIntro.cn: faulty 意为运转不正常、存在缺陷，或建立在错误想法上。

core.en: Something that contains a defect and therefore cannot be trusted.
core.cn: 含有缺陷、因而不可信赖的事物。

branches.en: A device that will not work correctly.
branches.cn: 无法正常工作的装置。

branches.en: A plan or structure with a weakness.
branches.cn: 存在弱点的计划或结构。

branches.en: A judgment built on a mistake.
branches.cn: 建立在错误之上的判断。

branches.en: A bad wire and a bad memory both mislead us.
branches.cn: 坏掉的电线与不可靠的记忆都会误导我们。

branches.en: The defect may be in the working part or in the design.
branches.cn: 缺陷可能出现在运转部件，也可能出在设计上。

intro.en: Faulty belongs to a family built on fault with suffixes of defect and perfection.
intro.cn: faulty 属于以 fault 为核心、由缺陷与完美两类后缀构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere and fallita lie behind fault and faulty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 与 fallita 是 fault 和 faulty 的深层来源。

items.example: The fault was found in minutes.
The old machine has many faults.
items.exampleCN: 这台旧机器有许多毛病。

items.example: The faulty cable was cut out.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的电缆被剪掉了。

items.example: This unit is faultier than the last.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备比上一台毛病更多。

items.example: That was the faultiest batch we tested.
items.exampleCN: 那是我们测试过问题最多的一批。

items.example: The test measured the faultiness of the seal.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量密封件的缺陷程度。

items.meaning: the state of having no faults
items.example: No one expects faultlessness in a first draft.
items.exampleCN: 没人指望初稿毫无瑕疵。

latinEntries.meaning: to deceive or cause to fail

definition_zh: 段落；段；报刊短讯；把……分段
definition_en: a group of sentences that develop one idea, a short separate item in a newspaper, and to divide a piece of writing into such groups
core_image: 一页稿纸上，红笔在句子之间划出几道横线
scene: 编辑把稿子摊在桌上，用红笔在需要停顿的地方画一道线。 She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
sceneCN: 这里 paragraph 是「段落」（第 1 个义项：文章里围绕一个意思的一组句子）；句意为她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。图中可辨识物件：稿纸、红笔、页边的横线。

derivatives.zh: 由 paragraph 加 -ing 构成，指分段的处理方式或页面上分段的样子
由 paragraph 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，指与段落有关的

senses.title: A group of sentences on one idea
senses.definition: a group of sentences that develop a single idea and are separated from the next group by a line break or an indent
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个意思展开的一组句子，与下一组之间以换行或缩进隔开
senses.example: She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。
senses.why: Greek paragraphos named a stroke written beside a line to mark a break; the mark then gave its name to the block of text it introduced.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 paragraphos 指在文字旁边画出、用来标示停顿的一道笔迹；后来这个记号就指它引出的那一段文字。

senses.title: A short item in a newspaper
senses.definition: a short separate item of news or comment in a newspaper, often only a few sentences long
senses.definitionCN: 报纸上独立成条的一小段新闻或评论，常常只有几句话
senses.example: The local paper ran a short paragraph about the missing cat.
senses.exampleCN: 地方报纸登了一小段关于那只走失的猫的消息。
senses.why: Because the mark cut a page into small blocks, the word could name any small block of print, and news writing soon used it for a brief item.
senses.whyCN: 因为这道记号把页面切成小块，这个词也就能指任何一小块印刷文字，新闻写作很快用它来指一条短讯。

senses.title: To divide writing into paragraphs
senses.definition: to arrange a piece of writing in paragraphs, or to mark the places where new paragraphs begin
senses.definitionCN: 把一篇文字安排成若干段落，或标出另起一段的位置
senses.example: He paragraphed the report carefully so that each claim stood alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他仔细地把报告分段，让每一条主张各占一段。
senses.why: Once the noun named the block, the verb followed by the usual English route: to paragraph is to cut a text into those blocks.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指段落这个块，动词就顺着英语常见的路子跟上来了：paragraph 就是按这些块把文字切开。

intro.en: Paragraph goes back to Greek words for beside and to write; the original thing was a mark in the margin, and the text it introduced borrowed the name.
intro.cn: paragraph 上溯到希腊语中表示「在旁边」与「写」的两个词；最初指的是页边的一个记号，后来它引出的那段文字借用了这个名字。

items.en: Para meant beside, and graphein meant to write or to scratch; a paragraphos was a stroke set beside a line of writing.
items.cn: para 意为在旁边，graphein 意为写、刻画；paragraphos 就是写在文字行旁的一道笔迹。

items.en: The noun came to mean not only the mark but the passage that the mark set off, a shift from sign to the thing signified.
items.cn: 这个名词后来不仅指记号，也指记号所分隔出的那一段文字，是从符号转向所指之物的变化。

items.en: Late Latin paragraphus and French paragraphe carried the term westward as a word of writing, copying and law.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 paragraphus 与法语的 paragraphe 把这个术语向西传播，用于书写、抄录与法律文书。

items.en: English paragraph first named the marginal mark, then the section of text that followed it.
items.cn: 英语里的 paragraph 先指页边的记号，随后指记号之后的那一节文字。

items.en: Modern English uses paragraph for a block of prose, for a short news item, and as a verb for dividing text.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paragraph 指散文中的一段、报刊上的一条短讯，也作动词表示把文字分段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Greek compounds that begin with the same short element, and each one attaches it to a different stem; the near-meaning group gathers other units of written text.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以那个短小成分开头的希腊复合词，但每个词接的词干都不同；近义组收其他表示文本单位的词。

entries.definition: Greek para plus allelos, one another; the two words share a prefix but are separate formations.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 allelos（彼此）；两词前缀写法相同，却是各自独立的构词，不是同一词族。

entries.definition: Para beside plus doxa opinion, a statement that sits against common belief.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 doxa（意见），指与常见看法相左的说法。

entries.definition: Para beside plus phrasis wording, a rewording of a text.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 phrasis（说法），指对原文的改写。

entries.definition: Para beside plus sitos food, one who eats at another person's table.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 sitos（食物），指在别人桌边吃饭的寄生者。

entries.definition: A short section of a book or a speech.
One of the parts into which a whole is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 整体被分成的部分之一。

entries.definition: A group of words that expresses a complete thought.
entries.definitionCN: 表达一个完整意思的一组词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek compound whose first half means beside; what it originally named was a mark, and English keeps both the mark and the block of text.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语复合词，前半意为「在旁边」；它最初命名的是一个记号，英语至今同时保留记号与那段文字两层意思。

normal.en: The Greek parts are para, beside, and graphein, to write: a paragraph began as a mark written beside the text.
normal.cn: 希腊部件是 para（在旁边）与 graphein（写）：paragraph 原本是写在文字旁边的一道记号。

normal.en: The mark gave its name to the sentences it introduced, which is why the word now means the text block itself.
normal.cn: 这道记号把自己的名字给了它引出的那几句，所以今天这个词指的是文字块本身。

normal.en: Paragraphing is the noun for the way a page is divided, and the -ing form keeps the action in view.
normal.cn: paragraphing 是表示「分段方式」的名词，-ing 形式让动作保持在视野里。

normal.en: The para- in paragraph hooks onto a verb of writing, while the para- in parallel belongs to a word for one another; they look alike but are separate formations.
normal.cn: paragraph 的 para- 接的是表示「写」的动词，parallel 的 para- 接的是表示「彼此」的词；两者看着一样，却是独立的两套构词。

normal.en: A newspaper paragraph is short because it is one small block of print on a crowded page.
normal.cn: 报纸上的 paragraph 之所以短，因为它是拥挤版面上的一小块印刷文字。

abstract.en: A paragraph is a pause made visible: the eye rests where the writer decided to stop.
abstract.cn: 段落是让停顿可见：目光停在作者决定收住的地方。

abstract.en: Cutting a page into blocks lends order to thought before the thought is fully clear.
abstract.cn: 把页面切成块，是在想法还没完全清楚之前先给它一个次序。

abstract.en: Two words can share four letters and still come from different rooms of the same language.
abstract.cn: 两个词可以共用四个字母，却仍来自同一种语言里不同的房间。

examples.en: She moved the last sentence into a new paragraph and read the page again.
examples.cn: 她把最后一句移到新的一段，又把这一页重读了一遍。

examples.en: The local paper ran a short paragraph about the missing cat.
examples.cn: 地方报纸登了一小段关于那只走失的猫的消息。

examples.en: He paragraphed the report carefully so that each claim stood alone.
examples.cn: 他仔细地把报告分段，让每一条主张各占一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍了个拉夫」——写完一段拍拍手，翻篇再写；记住 paragraph 是段落。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁边）加 graphein（写），paragraphos 原指写在行旁表示停顿的记号，后指记号引出的那段文字，经晚期拉丁语与法语进入英语。它与 parallel 虽然都写作 para-，却是两套各自独立的希腊构词，并非同源词族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a break marked in a text; the senses run from the block of sentences, to a short newspaper item, to the verb for cutting prose into such blocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是文本中被标出的一次停顿；义项从一组句子，走到报刊上的短讯，再到把文字切成这种块的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line drawn down the margin, marking where the reader may pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：页边画下的一道红线，标出读者可以换气的地方。

branches.en: a red stroke in the margin of a manuscript
branches.cn: 手稿页边的一道红线

branches.en: a page where each idea gets its own block
branches.cn: 每个意思各占一块的页面

branches.en: a few lines about a lost cat in the local paper
branches.cn: 地方报纸上关于走失小猫的几行字

branches.en: an editor splitting a long report by hand
branches.cn: 编辑亲手把长报告分段

branches.en: a writer deciding where the reader may breathe
branches.cn: 作者决定读者在哪里换气

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of a preposition and a verb of writing, filtered through Latin and French, and English adds its own endings to it.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中一个介词与一个「写」的动词拼成的复合词，经拉丁语与法语过滤后进入英语，英语又给它加上自己的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; late Latin paragraphus is itself a borrowing of the Greek noun, and the English word came by way of French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；晚期拉丁语的 paragraphus 本身是对希腊名词的借用，英语词则经由法语传来。

items.meaning: a stroke written beside a line
the way a text is divided
the sign that starts a new paragraph

definition_zh: 坟墓；墓穴；严重的
definition_en: a place where a body is buried, or very serious
core_image: 一块灰色墓碑立在长满青草的坡上
scene: 山坡上有一座安静的坟墓。 There is a quiet grave on the hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 grave 是「坟墓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：山坡上有一座安静的坟墓。

senses.title: A burial place
senses.definition: a place in the ground where a body is buried
senses.definitionCN: 地下埋葬遗体的地方
senses.example: There is a quiet grave on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 山坡上有一座安静的坟墓。
senses.why: The burial place is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 埋葬之地是最古老的具体义。

senses.title: Very serious
senses.definition: very serious and worrying
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重且令人担忧的
senses.example: The patient is in grave danger.
senses.exampleCN: 病人处于严重危险之中。
senses.why: A heavy matter is felt as a serious one.
senses.whyCN: 沉重之事，被感受为严重之事。

senses.title: Solemn in manner
senses.definition: serious and solemn in manner
senses.definitionCN: 举止严肃而庄重的
senses.example: He spoke in a grave voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他用严肃的声音说话。
senses.why: The serious sense moves from events to people.
senses.whyCN: 严重之义从事态转到人的神态。

intro.en: Grave has two roots: a dug pit and the Latin word for heavy.
intro.cn: grave 有两条词源：挖掘出的坑，以及拉丁语中「沉重」一词。

items.en: Grafan meant to dig.
items.cn: grafan 意为挖掘。

items.en: Græf named a dug burial pit.
items.cn: græf 指挖出的墓坑。

items.en: Grave kept the burial and digging sense.
items.cn: grave 保留了埋葬与挖掘之义。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy or serious.
items.cn: gravis 意为沉重的、严重的。

items.en: Grave as an adjective named seriousness.
items.cn: 作形容词的 grave 表示严肃、严重。

note.en: Grave is compared with look-alike words and words for tombs and seriousness.
note.cn: 把 grave 与形近词以及表示坟墓、严肃的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small round fruit
a diagram of data
small stones
a stone grave or monument
very bad or important
very serious and formal

normalIntro.en: Grave is both a quiet place and a heavy word.
normalIntro.cn: grave 既是一处安静之地，也是一个沉重的词。

normal.en: Flowers lay on the grave.
normal.cn: 墓上放着花。

normal.en: They visited the family grave.
normal.cn: 他们去扫了家族的墓。

normal.en: The news is grave.
normal.cn: 消息很严重。

normal.en: He spoke in a grave tone.
normal.cn: 他用严肃的语气说话。

normal.en: This is a grave mistake.
normal.cn: 这是一个重大错误。

abstract.en: A grave is a door the living cannot open.
abstract.cn: 坟墓，是活人打不开的门。

abstract.en: Heavy words are spoken slowly.
abstract.cn: 沉重的话，说得慢。

abstract.en: The stone keeps a name longer than memory does.
abstract.cn: 石头留名，比记忆更久。

examples.en: There is a quiet grave on the hillside.
examples.cn: 山坡上有一座安静的坟墓。

examples.en: The patient is in grave danger.
examples.cn: 病人处于严重危险之中。

examples.en: He spoke in a grave voice.
examples.cn: 他用严肃的声音说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: grave 作名词是「坟墓」，作形容词是「严重的、严肃的」；grave danger 是严重危险，grave mistake 是重大错误；副词 gravely、名词 gravity 同源。

root: 名词义来自古英语 græf（挖出的坑），与 grafan（挖掘）同源；形容词义来自拉丁语 gravis（沉重的），核心义为「沉重」，引申为严重与庄重。

sensesIntro.en: Grave means a burial place, something very serious, or a solemn manner.
sensesIntro.cn: grave 指坟墓、非常严重的事，或严肃的举止。

core.en: A dug place, and a weight on the mind.
core.cn: 一处挖出的地方，以及心上的重量。

branches.en: A spade turns dark soil.
branches.cn: 铁锹翻起黑土。

branches.en: A doctor lowers her voice.
branches.cn: 医生压低了声音。

branches.en: A speaker stands still before the crowd.
branches.cn: 说话者在人群前站定。

branches.en: The place and the manner share a silence.
branches.cn: 地方与神态，共用一种沉默。

branches.en: Weight in events becomes weight in voice.
branches.cn: 事态的沉重，变成声音的沉重。

intro.en: Grave forms plurals, comparison, adverbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: grave 构成复数、比较级、副词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: The adjective grave goes back to Latin gravis, heavy.
latinIntro.cn: 形容词 grave 可追溯到拉丁语 gravis，意为沉重。

items.example: The graveness of the case was clear.
An old graveyard lies behind the church.
items.exampleCN: 教堂后面有一片古老的墓地。

definition_zh: 含酒精的；酗酒者；酒精依赖者
definition_en: containing alcohol, or a person who cannot control their drinking
core_image: 一只杯子上贴着成分标签，另一只杯子被推到了一边
scene: 聚会上有人把杯子轻轻推开，另拿了一瓶没有标签的饮料。 He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
sceneCN: 这里 alcoholic 是「含酒精的」（第 1 个义项：饮料中含有乙醇）；句意为他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、无标签瓶子、餐巾。

pos.zh: 形容词：含酒精的；与酗酒有关的
名词：酗酒者；酒精依赖者

derivatives.zh: 本词的名词词根，义为「酒精；乙醇」
由本词词根加名词后缀构成，义为「酒精依赖；酗酒成瘾」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: Containing alcohol
senses.definition: of a drink, containing ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 指饮料中含有乙醇
senses.example: He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。
senses.why: The -ic ending turns the substance into an adjective, so alcoholic simply means 'having the quality of alcohol'.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ic 把物质变成形容词，所以 alcoholic 就是「带有酒精性质的」。

senses.title: A person dependent on alcohol
senses.definition: a person who is unable to control their drinking and depends on alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 无法控制饮酒、对酒精产生依赖的人
senses.example: The clinic offers support for alcoholics and their families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为酗酒者及其家人提供支持。
senses.why: Medical writing turned the adjective into a noun for a patient, which is why the word can sound clinical rather than insulting.
senses.whyCN: 医学文献把这个形容词转成指病人的名词，所以这个词听起来偏临床，而不一定是辱骂。

intro.en: Alcoholic is a nineteenth-century medical coinage: the Arabic-derived noun alcohol plus the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: alcoholic 是十九世纪的医学新造词：由阿拉伯语来源的名词 alcohol 加上形容词词尾 -ic。

items.en: The Arabic word named a fine powder and later, through alchemy, a distilled spirit.
items.cn: 这个阿拉伯词原指细粉，后来经炼金术转指蒸馏酒。

items.en: Alchemists used alcohol for any finely purified substance, especially distilled liquid.
items.cn: 炼金术士用 alcohol 指任何精细提纯之物，尤指蒸馏液。

items.en: By the eighteenth century English alcohol meant the intoxicating substance in wine and beer.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，英语 alcohol 已指葡萄酒与啤酒中致醉的物质。

items.en: The adjective alcoholic is coined in medical writing, and the noun for the patient follows soon after.
items.cn: 形容词 alcoholic 在医学文献中被造出，指病人的名词随后出现。

items.en: The adjective widened to any drink containing ethanol, while the noun kept its clinical force.
items.cn: 形容词扩展指任何含乙醇的饮品，名词则保留临床意味。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the alcohol family; the near-meaning group gathers words for strong drink and for people who depend on it.
note.cn: 形近组收 alcohol 词族；近义组收烈酒与依赖酒精者的说法。

entries.definition: The substance itself, ethanol.
The condition of dependence on alcohol.
A related chemical class, named from alcohol minus hydrogen.
entries.definitionCN: 一类相关化合物，名称由 alcohol 减氢缩合而成。

entries.definition: Capable of making someone drunk.
An informal and often critical word for someone who drinks too much.
entries.definitionCN: 对酗酒者带批评意味的口语说法。

entries.definition: Strong distilled drinks considered as a category.

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the noun alcohol and the adjective ending -ic.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：名词 alcohol 与形容词词尾 -ic。

normal.en: Alcohol plus -ic makes the adjective; the same -ic appears in acidic and heroic.
normal.cn: alcohol 加 -ic 构成形容词，acidic、heroic 里的也是同一个 -ic。

normal.en: As a noun it names a patient, so it is better avoided as an insult.
normal.cn: 作名词时它指病人，因此不宜拿来骂人。

normal.en: Non-alcoholic keeps the prefix visible: non- plus alcoholic.
normal.cn: non-alcoholic 里前缀仍然看得见：non- 加 alcoholic。

normal.en: The stress falls on -hol: al-co-HOL-ic.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -hol 上：al-co-HOL-ic。

normal.en: Keep the h: alco-holic, not alco-olic.
normal.cn: 不要丢掉 h：alco-holic，而不是 alco-olic。

abstract.en: One suffix turns a substance into a person, which shows how easily medical language labels an identity.
abstract.cn: 一个词尾把一种物质变成一个人，说明医学语言多容易给人贴上身份标签。

abstract.en: The adjective describes a drink; the noun describes a life, and the gap between them is the whole social weight of the word.
abstract.cn: 形容词描述一杯饮料，名词描述一种人生，两者之间的落差就是这个词的全部分量。

abstract.en: Because the word is clinical, saying it about someone carries a diagnosis rather than an opinion.
abstract.cn: 由于这个词带临床色彩，用它说某个人，等于给出诊断而不是意见。

examples.en: He ordered an alcoholic drink, then changed his mind.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯含酒精的饮料，后来又改了主意。

examples.en: The clinic offers support for alcoholics and their families.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为酗酒者及其家人提供支持。

examples.en: The hotel bar serves both alcoholic and soft drinks.
examples.cn: 酒店酒吧既供应含酒精饮料，也供应软饮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱扣喝立刻」——爱扣着杯子喝，立刻就上了瘾。

root: 由 alcohol「酒精」加形容词词尾 -ic 构成，十九世纪医学用语，后兼指酒精依赖者。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from one substance: the adjective describes a drink that contains it, the noun describes a person controlled by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都出自同一种物质：形容词描述含有它的饮料，名词描述被它控制的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one glass labelled with its contents, another glass quietly pushed aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只标着成分的杯子，另一只被悄悄推到一边。

branches.en: a bottle with a percentage on the label
branches.cn: 标签上标着度数的瓶子

branches.en: a menu divided into soft and strong
branches.cn: 分成软饮与烈酒两栏的酒单

branches.en: a chair in a support group circle
branches.cn: 互助小组围坐的一把椅子

branches.en: a hospital chart with a diagnosis
branches.cn: 写着诊断的病房记录

branches.en: one substance, described first as a quality and then as a fate
branches.cn: 同一种物质，先被描述为一种性质，再被描述为一种命运

intro.en: The noun alcohol, its Arabic source, and the adjective ending that turns it into a description.
intro.cn: 名词 alcohol、它的阿拉伯语来源，以及把它变成描述性词语的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Latin from Arabic; the list gives the Arabic elements and the Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从阿拉伯语进入拉丁语；列表中给出阿拉伯语成分与拉丁语形式。

definition_zh: 危险；隐患；公害；冒险猜测
definition_en: something that could cause harm, or to risk a guess
core_image: 路面上被薄冰盖住的一道裂缝
scene: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。 The wet floor is a hazard.
sceneCN: 这里 hazard 是「隐患」（第 1 个义项）；句意：湿滑的地面是个隐患。

senses.title: A source of danger
senses.definition: something that could cause harm or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害或事故的事物
senses.example: The wet floor is a hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a hidden risk.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示潜在危险的义项。

senses.title: Risk a guess
senses.definition: to say or try something without being sure
senses.definitionCN: 没有把握地说出或尝试某事
senses.example: He hazarded a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 他大胆猜了一下。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of taking a chance.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为冒险一试的行为。

senses.title: A public danger
senses.definition: a danger to health or safety in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某处对健康或安全的危害
senses.example: Smoke is a health hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 烟雾是健康危害。
senses.why: The risk becomes a named public problem.
senses.whyCN: 风险变成了被点名的公共问题。

intro.en: Hazard entered English through Old French as a dice game.
intro.cn: hazard 经古法语进入英语，最初指一种掷骰游戏。

items.en: The word may come from an Arabic word for dice.
items.cn: 这个词可能来自阿拉伯语中表示骰子的词。

items.en: Hasard named a game of dice.
items.cn: hasard 指一种掷骰游戏。

items.en: Hazard meant chance or luck in a game.
items.cn: hazard 指游戏中的偶然与运气。

items.en: Hazard shifted to mean danger or risk.
items.cn: hazard 转指危险或风险。

items.en: Hazard also named a source of harm.
items.cn: hazard 也指危害的来源。

note.en: Hazard is compared with look-alike words and with words for danger.
note.cn: 把 hazard 与形近词以及表示危险的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small nut tree
not clear because of mist
done too quickly
the chance of harm
the possibility of loss
great danger

normalIntro.en: Hazard is harm waiting to happen.
normalIntro.cn: hazard 是随时可能发生的伤害。

normal.en: Wet floors are a hazard.
normal.cn: 湿滑的地面是隐患。

normal.en: Smoke is a health hazard.
normal.cn: 烟雾是健康危害。

normal.en: They cleared every fire hazard.
normal.cn: 他们清除了所有火灾隐患。

normal.en: He hazarded a guess.
normal.cn: 他大胆猜了一下。

normal.en: The sign marks the hazard.
normal.cn: 标牌标出了危险处。

abstract.en: A hazard is a shadow cast by a possible accident.
abstract.cn: 隐患，是可能事故投下的影子。

abstract.en: Name the hazard and it shrinks.
abstract.cn: 把隐患说出来，它就变小了。

abstract.en: Luck and hazard share one die.
abstract.cn: 运气与危险共用同一颗骰子。

examples.en: The wet floor is a hazard.
examples.cn: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。

examples.en: He hazarded a guess.
examples.cn: 他大胆猜了一下。

examples.en: Smoke is a health hazard.
examples.cn: 烟雾是健康危害。

dict_mnemonic.text: hazard 是「危险、隐患」；health hazard 是健康危害，fire hazard 是火灾隐患，hazard a guess 是壮着胆子猜一猜。

root: 经古法语 hasard（掷骰游戏）进入英语，词源或可追溯至阿拉伯语中表示骰子的词；由赌局中的偶然与运气，转指危险与风险。

sensesIntro.en: Hazard is a source of harm, a health danger, or the act of risking a guess.
sensesIntro.cn: hazard 是危害源、健康隐患，或冒险猜测的行为。

core.en: A hidden edge where harm may start.
core.cn: 伤害可能开始的一道暗边。

branches.en: The wet floor is a hazard.
branches.cn: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。

branches.en: He hazarded a guess.
branches.cn: 他大胆猜了一下。

branches.en: Smoke is a health hazard.
branches.cn: 烟雾是健康危害。

branches.en: A small risk becomes a public danger.
branches.cn: 小小的风险会变成公共的危害。

branches.en: To guess at hazard is to roll the dice.
branches.cn: 冒险一猜，就是在掷骰子。

intro.en: Hazard takes suffixes for danger and compounds for warnings.
intro.cn: hazard 加后缀表示危险，并构成警示类复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是经古法语传入的。

items.meaning: a dice game, later a risk

items.exampleCN: 危险废物需要谨慎处理。

definition_zh: 鞭子；抽打；（快速）搅打（奶油、蛋）；(议会)党鞭
definition_en: a long thin strip of leather on a handle, used to strike animals, and the quick beating motion made with it
core_image: 一条皮鞭在空中甩出一个急速的弧线
scene: 马厩前，骑手抬手一甩，皮鞭在空气里划出弧形的响声，马立刻加快脚步。 The driver cracked the whip and the horses ran faster.
sceneCN: 这里 whip 是「鞭子」（第 1 个义项：带柄的长皮条，用来抽打牲畜）；句意为车夫甩响鞭子，马跑得更快了。皮鞭在空中甩出急速弧线的画面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 抽打；快速搅打；猛地移动

senses.title: The leather tool
senses.definition: a long thin strip of leather or cord fixed to a handle, used for striking
senses.definitionCN: 固定在柄上的细长皮带或绳索，用来抽打
senses.example: The driver cracked the whip and the horses ran faster.
senses.exampleCN: 车夫甩响鞭子，马跑得更快了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the object itself, which was first a quick-moving instrument for driving animals.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是这件物体本身，起初是一种快速挥动、用来驱使牲畜的工具。

senses.title: To strike with it
senses.definition: to hit a person or animal with a whip, or as if with one
senses.definitionCN: 用鞭子或仿佛用鞭子击打人或动物
senses.example: The rain whipped against the windows all night.
senses.exampleCN: 雨整夜抽打着窗户。
senses.why: The verb came straight from the noun, and from hitting it widened to anything that hits sharply and fast.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接由名词而来，从击打又扩展到任何迅猛而尖锐的拍打。

senses.title: To beat food quickly
senses.definition: to beat cream, eggs or a mixture quickly with a fork or whisk until air is folded in
senses.definitionCN: 用叉子或打蛋器快速搅打奶油、蛋或混合物，使空气混入
senses.example: Whip the cream until it holds soft peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 把奶油搅打至能形成柔软的尖角。
senses.why: The fast circular motion of a whip in the air is the same motion as a whisk in a bowl.
senses.whyCN: 鞭子在空中甩出的快速绕圈动作，与打蛋器在碗里的动作完全相同。

senses.title: To move suddenly
senses.definition: to move or take something out suddenly and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 突然而迅速地移动或抽出某物
senses.example: She whipped out her phone and took a photo.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地掏出手机拍了一张。
senses.why: The curve of a cracking whip is a picture of pure speed, so the verb took on the meaning to move in that shape.
senses.whyCN: 甩响的鞭子那一道弧线就是纯粹的速度，于是动词也带上了那样移动的意思。

senses.title: The party official
senses.definition: in a parliament, the member whose job is to keep the party together and see that members vote
senses.definitionCN: 在议会中负责维持本党团结、督促议员投票的成员
senses.example: The chief whip warned the party not to split.
senses.exampleCN: 党鞭长警告党内不要分裂。
senses.why: A hunting term for the rider who keeps the hounds together was borrowed for the official who rounds up votes.
senses.whyCN: 一个狩猎术语指把猎犬聚拢起来的骑手，后来借指把选票聚集起来的官员。

intro.en: Whip comes from Middle English wippen, to swing or snatch quickly, and the noun for the tool followed.
intro.cn: whip 源自中古英语 wippen（快速挥动或抓取），表示工具的义项随之出现。

items.en: The family of fast-moving words included the ancestors of whip and of wippen in other Germanic tongues.
items.cn: 这个表示快速动作的词族包含 whip 在其他日耳曼语言中的祖先形式。

items.en: Wippen meant to move nimbly or to snatch, and the noun wippe named the swinging tool.
items.cn: wippen 意为轻快移动或抓取，名词 wippe 指挥动的工具。

items.en: The verb covered beating, whipping and the fast beating of cream, and hunting gave the word its pack sense.
items.cn: 动词涵盖抽打、鞭打与快速搅打奶油，狩猎语境又给了它「成群领袖」的意思。

items.en: Industry made whiplash and whip-round part of everyday speech, and the adjective whippy followed.
items.cn: 工业与日常生活让 whiplash、whip-round 成为常用语，形容词 whippy 也随之出现。

items.en: Parliamentary usage fixed the political whip in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 议会用法在十九世纪把政治意义上的 whip 固定下来。

note.en: The first group is the look-alike words that differ by one sound, the second the words that also mean to hit or to beat food.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个音的近形词，第二组是同样表示击打或搅打的说法。

entries.definition: A thin twisting strand, as of smoke or straw.
The hand that holds the whip, and so the advantage.
To clean with a cloth, one vowel apart.
A small piece broken off; a different opening sound.
To strike with the end of a whip, and the cord itself.
The general verb for stirring or hitting hard.
The kitchen tool for whipping, and to move it fast.
To beat someone severely as a punishment.

normalIntro.en: Every sense of whip comes from one picture: a thin strip travelling very fast through the air.
normalIntro.cn: whip 的每个义项都出自同一幅画面：一条细长的皮条极快地穿破空气。

normal.en: The wh of the crack is in the word: whip sounds like the strike.
normal.cn: 甩鞭的响声就在词里：whip 听起来就像那一下抽打。

normal.en: Air, horse, cream, phone: the same fast curve in four places.
normal.cn: 空气、马背、奶油、手机：同一个快速弧线用在四处。

normal.en: To whip up a meal is to make it in the time of one crack.
normal.cn: whip up 一顿饭就是用一下响鞭的时间做出来。

normal.en: The party whip rounds up votes the way a huntsman rounds up hounds.
normal.cn: 党鞭聚拢选票，就像猎手聚拢猎犬。

normal.en: Double the p before -ed and -ing: whipped, whipping.
normal.cn: 在 -ed 和 -ing 前要双写 p：whipped、whipping。

abstract.en: Hear a sharp crack and then the beat of hooves.
abstract.cn: 听一声脆响和随后急促的马蹄声。

abstract.en: See a thin line bending in the air.
abstract.cn: 想一条细线在空气中弯折。

abstract.en: Feel the sting that arrives a moment later.
abstract.cn: 感受稍后才到的火辣辣的痛。

examples.en: He keeps a long leather whip on the wall.
examples.cn: 他墙上挂着一根长皮鞭。

examples.en: Whip the eggs with a little sugar.
examples.cn: 把鸡蛋加少许糖搅打一下。

examples.en: The wind whipped the flags above the gate.
examples.cn: 风把门上的旗子抽得猎猎作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威扑」——威风一扑，皮鞭抽出一条弧线。

root: 中古英语 wippen（快速挥动、抓取）→ whip；同族有 whiplash、whipping、whip-round。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a fast-moving tool, becomes the act of striking with it, then the fast beating of food, then any sudden movement, and finally the official who keeps a party in line.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一件快速挥动的工具开始，变成用它的击打，再变成快速搅打食物，再变成任何迅猛的动作，最后指维持本党一致的官员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leather strip drawn fast through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条皮条急速抽过空气。

branches.en: The object branch: the driver cracks the whip.
branches.cn: 物体分支：车夫甩响鞭子。

branches.en: The strike branch: rain whipping the windows.
branches.cn: 击打分支：雨抽打窗户。

branches.en: The kitchen branch: whipping cream to soft peaks.
branches.cn: 厨房分支：把奶油打至软尖。

branches.en: The speed branch: whipping out a phone.
branches.cn: 速度分支：猛地掏出手机。

branches.en: The political branch: the chief whip warns the party.
branches.cn: 政治分支：党鞭长警告全党。

intro.en: Whip is a whole Germanic word, and it grows by compounding and by phrases rather than by prefixes.
intro.cn: whip 是一个完整的日耳曼词，它靠复合与短语生长，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used flagellum for the tool and verbera for the blows; the entries below are borrowed counterparts, not ancestors of whip.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 flagellum 指鞭子，用 verbera 指鞭打；下面的条目是借入的对应词，并非 whip 的祖先。

items.example: The same word is tool and action.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词既是工具也是动作。

items.example: It also means to stir up feeling.
It turns the sound into a metaphor.
It refers to the rein hand.

definition_zh: 加宽；拓宽；扩大；（差距）拉大；睁大
definition_en: to make something broader, or to become broader, and figuratively to increase a range or a gap
core_image: 一条原本只容一人通过的小路，被两边的铁锹一点点挖宽
scene: 工人们沿着小路两侧挖土，把路面一点点加宽，好让手推车也能过去。 They plan to widen the road before the summer holidays.
sceneCN: 这里 widen 是「加宽」（第 1 个义项：使某物从一边到另一边的距离变大）；句意为他们打算在暑假前把这条路加宽。两把铁锹把窄路一点点挖宽，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 加宽；拓宽；扩大；变得更大

senses.title: To make physically broader
senses.definition: to increase the width of a road, a hole or a passage
senses.definitionCN: 增大道路、洞口或通道的宽度
senses.example: They plan to widen the road before the summer holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打算在暑假前把这条路加宽。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the adjective into action on a piece of ground or stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把形容词的宽度落实到一段地面或石块上。

senses.title: To become broader
senses.definition: to grow wider by itself, without anyone making it happen
senses.definitionCN: 自身变宽变大，并非由人推动
senses.example: The river widens as it reaches the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 河流到了平原就变宽了。
senses.why: English often uses the same verb for doing and for happening, and here the road does it to itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让同一个动词兼顾「做」与「发生」，这里路自己变宽了。

senses.title: To enlarge a range
senses.definition: to make a set of things, people or chances larger
senses.definitionCN: 使事物、人物或机会的集合变大
senses.example: Reading in two languages will widen your experience.
senses.exampleCN: 用两种语言阅读会拓宽你的阅历。
senses.why: A wider field holds more, so stretching a range is the same motion applied to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 更宽的场地能容纳更多，所以扩大范围就是把同一个动作用在想法上。

senses.title: To increase a gap
senses.definition: used of a distance or difference between two sides that grows larger
senses.definitionCN: 指两方之间的距离或差别变得更大
senses.example: The gap between the two teams widened after the second goal.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个球之后，两队之间的差距拉大了。
senses.why: The space between two points is stretched in the same way as a road, only nobody digs it.
senses.whyCN: 两点之间的空间被拉宽，和修路是一个动作，只是没人动手挖。

senses.title: Eyes growing round
senses.definition: used of eyes that open wider through surprise or fear
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛因惊讶或恐惧而睁得更大
senses.example: Her eyes widened when she heard the price.
senses.exampleCN: 听到价格时，她的眼睛睁大了。
senses.why: The eye opens sideways like a small road, and the same verb covers that move.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛像一条小路那样向两边打开，同一个动词也就覆盖了这个动作。

intro.en: Widen is a native verb built by adding the Old English ending -en to wid, broad, the same pattern that produced deepen and strengthen.
intro.cn: widen 是在「宽阔」的 wid 上加古英语词尾 -en 构成的本土动词，与 deepen、strengthen 是同一模式。

items.en: The ending -en turned adjectives into verbs meaning to make that quality, as in hwit becoming hwitnian.
items.cn: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成表示「使之具有该性质」的动词，如 hwit 变成 hwitnian。

items.en: Widnen appears in writing for making something broader, still close to its physical sense.
items.cn: 中古英语中 widnen 已用于表示加宽，仍贴近物理意义。

items.en: The spelling settled as widen, and the word spread from roads to ranges and to gaps.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 widen，这个词从道路扩展到范围与差距。

items.en: Abstract uses such as widen your experience became common in writing about education.
items.cn: widen your experience 一类抽象用法在教育写作中变得常见。

items.en: The eye-filling phrase eyes widened became a fixed image of surprise in modern prose.
items.cn: eyes widened 这一说法在现代散文里成了表示惊讶的固定形象。

note.en: The first group gathers the other -en verbs of the same kind, the second the verbs of making something larger.
note.cn: 第一组收同类的其他 -en 动词，第二组收表示扩大的动词。

entries.definition: To make or become deep.
To make or become strong.
The noun beside the verb.
The adjective the verb comes from.
To make broader, often of experience or outlook.
To grow larger in all directions.
To make longer or to reach further.

normalIntro.en: Widen is an -en verb, so its shape is simply the adjective with a verb ending attached.
normalIntro.cn: widen 是个 -en 动词，它的形状就是形容词后面接上一个动词词尾。

normal.en: Deep, strength and wide all take -en to become actions.
normal.cn: deep、strength、wide 都加 -en 变成动作。

normal.en: A road is widened with spades, a river widens on its own.
normal.cn: 路要靠铁锹加宽，河却自己变宽。

normal.en: Widen a gap and nobody digs, the distance just grows.
normal.cn: 拉大差距时没人动土，距离自己长大。

normal.en: Read two languages and your experience widens.
normal.cn: 读两种语言，阅历就拓宽了。

normal.en: Eyes widen before the mouth has time to speak.
normal.cn: 眼睛先睁大，嘴还没来得及说话。

abstract.en: See a narrow path slowly breathing outwards.
abstract.cn: 看见一条小路慢慢向两边舒展开。

abstract.en: Feel the two banks of a river step apart.
abstract.cn: 感觉河的两岸一步步让开。

abstract.en: Hear a range of choices grow until it reaches the wall.
abstract.cn: 听一个选择范围一直长到墙边。

examples.en: The council agreed to widen the bridge next spring.
examples.cn: 议会同意明年春天拓宽这座桥。

examples.en: The gap between rich and poor has widened again.
examples.cn: 贫富差距又一次拉大了。

examples.en: His eyes widened when the door opened by itself.
examples.cn: 门自己打开时，他的眼睛睁大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外的恩」——外面又得恩赐一块地，所以路宽了。

root: 古英语 wid（宽阔）+ 动词词尾 -en → 中古英语 widnen → 现代英语 widen；同族有 wide、width、widely。

sensesIntro.en: The verb makes a road broader, lets a river broaden itself, stretches a range of choices, opens a growing gap, and finally opens a pair of eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词把路加宽，让河自己变宽，拉开选择的范围，张开越变越大的差距，最后睁大一双眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two spades cutting a narrow path wider.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把铁锹把窄路一点点挖宽。

branches.en: The road branch: widening before the holidays.
branches.cn: 道路分支：假期前动工加宽。

branches.en: The river branch: the water spreading on the plain.
branches.cn: 河流分支：水在平原上散开。

branches.en: The experience branch: reading in two languages.
branches.cn: 阅历分支：用两种语言阅读。

branches.en: The gap branch: two teams drawing apart.
branches.cn: 差距分支：两支队伍越拉越远。

branches.en: The surprise branch: eyes opening at a price.
branches.cn: 惊讶分支：听到价格时睁大的眼睛。

intro.en: Widen is a good example of a productive suffix: -en on an adjective makes a verb meaning to make or become that way.
intro.cn: widen 是能产后缀的好例子：-en 加在形容词上，造出「使…或变得…」的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is native, but the same job is done in Latin by the suffix -are on adjectives; the entries below show borrowed verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土的，而拉丁语中由形容词加 -are 完成同样的工作；下面的条目展示借入的动词。

items.example: The abstract use of the verb.
A common frame in news writing.
items.exampleCN: 新闻写作中的常见框架。

latinEntries.example: It lies behind the English amplify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是英语 amplify 的来源。

definition_zh: 小提琴
definition_en: a small wooden instrument with four strings, played with a bow
core_image: 肩上架着一把琴，琴弓停在弦上的一瞬
scene: 排练厅里，首席把琴架上肩，弓子一落，整个乐队都跟着定下音来。 She tuned her violin before the orchestra began to play.
sceneCN: 这里 violin 是「小提琴」（第 1 个义项：四弦、以弓拉奏的小型木制乐器）；句意为乐团开演前她给小提琴调了音。肩上架琴、弓停在弦上的那一瞬正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小提琴手」
加后缀 -istic 构成，义为「小提琴演奏风格的」

senses.title: The four-stringed instrument played with a bow
senses.definition: a small bowed string instrument with four strings and a high voice
senses.definitionCN: 四弦、以弓拉奏、音色高亢的小型弦乐器
senses.example: She tuned her violin before the orchestra began to play.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团开演前她给小提琴调了音。
senses.why: Italian violino means a small viola, and smallness is exactly what makes it the leading voice.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 violino 意为「小维奥尔」，而正是它的小巧使它成为主导声部。

senses.title: The violin section of an orchestra
senses.definition: the group of players who play violins in an orchestra
senses.definitionCN: 乐团中演奏小提琴的一组人
senses.example: The violins came in a beat early.
senses.exampleCN: 小提琴声部早进了一拍。
senses.why: Orchestras name whole sections after the instrument, so violins can mean the players.
senses.whyCN: 乐团以乐器命名整个声部，于是 violins 也可指演奏的人。

senses.title: The violin part of a score
senses.definition: the line of music written for the instrument in a work
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲中写给这一乐器的谱线
senses.example: The violin enters alone in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章里小提琴独自进入。
senses.why: A score labels its lines by instrument, so the word also marks a place in the page.
senses.whyCN: 乐谱以乐器标注谱线，因此这个词也指页面上的那一行。

senses.title: The craft and trade of making violins
senses.definition: the instrument regarded as an object of fine craft
senses.definitionCN: 作为精细工艺品的这类乐器
senses.example: That violin was made in Cremona three centuries ago.
senses.exampleCN: 那把琴是三百年前在克雷莫纳制作的。
senses.why: Some instruments outlive players and become objects of craft, and the word names them so.
senses.whyCN: 有些乐器比演奏者更长寿，成为工艺对象，这个词就用来称呼它们。

senses.title: In idiom, the second place after the leader
senses.definition: the position of playing second to another, in the phrase second fiddle or second violin
senses.definitionCN: 在「第二小提琴」一类说法中，指居于他人之后的位置
senses.example: He was happy to play second violin in the project.
senses.exampleCN: 他乐意在这个项目里打下手。
senses.why: Since the section has a leader, playing second violin became a picture of a lesser role.
senses.whyCN: 既然声部有首席，拉第二小提琴便成了次要角色的写照。

intro.en: Violin is Italian violino, a small viola, from Medieval Latin vitula, a stringed instrument.
intro.cn: violin 是意大利语 violino（小维奥尔），来自中世纪拉丁语 vitula（弦乐器）。

items.en: Vitula named a stringed instrument in late Latin.
items.cn: 后期的拉丁语中，vitula 指一种弦乐器。

items.en: The word passed into the Romance languages as viola, a bowed instrument.
items.cn: 该词进入罗曼语族作 viola，指弓弦乐器。

items.en: Italian added the diminutive -ino, giving violino, the small one.
items.cn: 意大利语加指小词尾 -ino，得 violino，即小的那种。

items.en: English borrowed violin in the seventeenth century with the new craft.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪随这门新工艺借入 violin。

items.en: The word covered both the instrument and its players in an orchestra.
items.cn: 这个词既指乐器，也指乐团里的演奏者。

note.en: The first group holds the violin family, the second the other bowed strings.
note.cn: 第一组是 violin 词族，第二组是其他弓弦乐器。

normalIntro.en: A small viola in Italian: the ending made the instrument and the instrument made the word.
normalIntro.cn: 意大利语里的「小维奥尔」：词尾造出乐器，乐器也定下这个词。

normal.en: Violin is Italian for a small viola.
normal.cn: violin 就是意大利语里的「小维奥尔」。

normal.en: Add -ist for violinist, the player.
normal.cn: 加 -ist 得 violinist，演奏者。

normal.en: The stress falls at the end: vi-o-LIN.
normal.cn: 重音在末尾：vi-o-LIN。

normal.cn: 乐器前要加定冠词：play the violin。

normal.en: Violet and violin share letters, not history.
normal.cn: violet 与 violin 只是字母相近，并无同源关系。

abstract.en: See a bow hovering one second above the strings.
abstract.cn: 想弓子在弦上方悬停一瞬。

abstract.en: Hear a single high note cut through an orchestra.
abstract.cn: 听一个高音穿透全团。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden body glowing under stage light.
abstract.cn: 想木琴身在灯光下发亮。

examples.en: He has played the violin since he was six.
examples.cn: 他六岁就开始拉小提琴。

examples.en: The violins carried the melody in the finale.
examples.cn: 终曲里旋律由小提琴声部承担。

examples.en: She teaches violin at the music school.
examples.cn: 她在音乐学校教小提琴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外俄林」——外面俄式林子里，有人拉起了小提琴。

root: 拉丁语 vitula（弦乐器）→ 中世纪拉丁语 viola → 意大利语 violino（小维奥尔）→ 英语 violin

sensesIntro.en: One instrument name stretches to cover its players, its lines in a score, its craft, and a modest place in a project.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个乐器名延伸去指演奏者、乐谱上的声部、制琴工艺，以及项目里的次要位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow resting still above four strings.
core.cn: 核心意象：弓子静停在四根弦上方。

branches.en: The rehearsal branch: tuning before the concert.
branches.cn: 排练分支：演出前调音。

branches.en: The section branch: the violins entering early.
branches.cn: 声部分支：小提琴声部早进一拍。

branches.en: The score branch: the violin alone in the slow movement.
branches.cn: 乐谱分支：慢乐章里小提琴独奏。

branches.en: The workshop branch: a Cremona violin of great age.
branches.cn: 工坊分支：克雷莫纳的老琴。

branches.en: The idiom branch: playing second in a project.
branches.cn: 习语分支：在项目里拉第二琴。

intro.en: The stem viol- plus the Italian diminutive -in makes violin; -ist names the player.
intro.cn: 词干 viol- 加意大利语指小词尾 -in 构成 violin，-ist 指演奏者。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitula became viola in the Romance languages; Italian shrank it with -ino, and English kept the form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitula 在罗曼语族成为 viola，意大利语以 -ino 缩小，英语沿用了这一形式。

items.example: The -in once meant a small viola.
Violinistic writing suits the high strings.

小提琴声部重新调了音。

definition_zh: 业余爱好者；业余的；外行的
definition_en: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than for money, or someone lacking professional skill
core_image: 周末公园里，一群爱好者扛着相机拍鸟
scene: 社区球场上，一群下班后赶来的球员换上球衣，没有一个人拿报酬。 The tournament is open to amateur players only.
sceneCN: 这里 amateur 是「业余的」（第 2 个义项：不以该项活动为职业、不取报酬）；句意是这项赛事只对业余选手开放。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：业余水平的；不够专业的
名词：业余主义；业余身份
形容词：爱情的，与 amateur 同源于拉丁语「爱」

senses.title: One who does it for love
senses.definition: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than as a job
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非职业参加某项活动的人
senses.example: He is a keen amateur photographer on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 他周末是个热心的业余摄影爱好者。
senses.why: The word goes back to Latin amator, 'lover', so an amateur is literally someone who does the activity for the love of it rather than for pay.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 amator「爱者」，所以 amateur 字面上就是因热爱而做某件事的人，而不是为报酬而做。

senses.title: Not professional
senses.definition: describing sport, art, or work done outside a profession and usually without payment
senses.definitionCN: 形容在职业体系之外进行、通常没有报酬的运动、艺术或工作
senses.example: The tournament is open to amateur players only.
senses.exampleCN: 这项赛事只对业余选手开放。
senses.why: Once amateur names the person, it can describe the whole level of activity, setting it against the paid professional circuit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 amateur 能指人，它也能形容整个活动层级，与有报酬的职业圈相对。

senses.title: A clumsy non-expert
senses.definition: a disapproving word for someone whose work shows lack of professional skill
senses.definitionCN: 带贬义，指工作显出缺乏专业训练的人
senses.example: The repairs were done by amateurs and soon fell apart.
senses.exampleCN: 这些维修是外行做的，很快就散架了。
senses.why: Because love without training can look clumsy, the word acquired a sneer: an amateur is not merely unpaid but unskilled.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有热爱而缺乏训练往往显得笨拙，这个词便带上讥讽：amateur 不只是没有报酬，还是技艺不精。

intro.en: Amateur is a love word: it descends from the Latin verb 'to love'.
intro.cn: amateur 是个与「爱」有关的词，源自拉丁语动词「爱」。

items.en: amare meant 'to love', the source of amatory and of amateur.
items.cn: amare 意为「爱」，是 amatory 与 amateur 的来源。

items.en: amator meant 'lover, one who loves', without any hint of incompetence.
items.cn: amator 意为「爱者、热爱者」，丝毫没有不专业的意思。

items.en: French amateur named someone who cultivates an art or sport for pleasure.
items.cn: 法语 amateur 指为兴趣而从事艺术或运动的人。

items.en: English adopted the word for the growing world of clubs, sports, and hobbies.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，用于兴起的俱乐部、运动与爱好圈子。

items.en: The disapproving sense 'unskilled' developed alongside the neutral one, so context decides the tone.
items.cn: 贬义的「不熟练」与中性的「业余」并行发展，语气由语境决定。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from the same root; the near-meaning group contrasts levels of skill and pay.
note.cn: 形近组同出一源；近义组对比技艺与报酬的层级。

the belief that sport should stay unpaid
entries.definitionCN: 主张运动不应职业化的理念

entries.definition: relating to love
one who pursues an interest in spare time
paid and trained in a field
a beginner

normalIntro.en: Amateur comes from love, not from lack.
normalIntro.cn: amateur 来自「爱」，而不是来自「缺少」。

normal.en: Latin amare means to love.
normal.cn: 拉丁 amare 意为爱。

normal.en: An amateur does it for love, a professional for pay.
normal.cn: 业余者为热爱而做，职业者为报酬而做。

normal.en: Amateurish is the adjective of disapproval.
normal.cn: amateurish 是带贬义的形容词。

normal.en: Amateur dramatics is a common British phrase.
normal.cn: amateur dramatics 是常见的英式说法。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AM-a-teur.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AM-a-teur。

abstract.en: Picture a weekend photographer with a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 想象周末背着沉重器材的摄影爱好者。

abstract.en: See a local team playing for fun.
abstract.cn: 想象本地队伍为乐趣而踢球。

abstract.en: Hear a critic calling the work amateurish.
abstract.cn: 听到评论者说这作品像外行做的。

examples.en: She plays tennis as an amateur, but she trains every morning.
examples.cn: 她以业余身份打网球，但每天早上都训练。

examples.en: The exhibition gives amateur artists a chance to show their work.
examples.cn: 这个展览给业余艺术家展示作品的机会。

examples.en: The wiring looked amateur and had to be redone.
examples.cn: 布线看起来很不专业，只好重做。

dict_mnemonic.text: amateur 与 amare「爱」同源：因热爱而做，不为报酬，就是业余。

root: 源自拉丁语 amare「爱」的派生词 amator「爱者」，经法语 amateur 于十八世纪进入英语，本指因热爱而从事某项活动的人，后发展出「非职业」与贬义的「外行」两层用法。

sensesIntro.en: Love of the activity yields three readings: the enthusiast, the unpaid level, and the unskilled outsider.
sensesIntro.cn: 对活动的热爱生出三种读法：爱好者、非职业层级、技艺不精的外行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weekend photographer who shoots for joy.
core.cn: 核心意象：为快乐而拍照的周末摄影者。

branches.en: a keen bird photographer
branches.cn: 热心的鸟类摄影者

branches.en: a local choir member
branches.cn: 本地合唱团成员

branches.cn: 业余戏剧

intro.en: A Latin love root with a small family of English derivatives.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁语「爱」的词根，带出一小族英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb amare and the noun amator are the source of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 amare 与名词 amator 是这一词族的来源。

items.meaning: one who does something for love

definition_zh: 模仿；仿效；照着做
definition_en: to copy the way someone speaks, moves, or behaves, or to copy the style of something, often in order to learn it or to make people laugh
core_image: 客厅里小男孩照着爸爸刮胡子的动作，对着镜子抹一脸泡沫
scene: 晚饭后客厅里，男孩举着爸爸的剃须刷，学着大人刮胡子的样子挥来挥去。 His little brother watched and tried to imitate every move.
sceneCN: 这里 imitate 是「模仿、仿效」（第 1 个义项：照着别人的动作或做法来），句意是弟弟在旁边看着，努力模仿他的每一个动作。画面里有晚饭后的客厅、一把剃须刷和一个学大人动作的小男孩。

pos.zh: 动词：模仿、仿效（某人的动作、声音、做法）；仿造、仿制

derivatives.zh: 无法模仿的、独一无二的

senses.title: To copy someone's actions
senses.titleCN: 模仿他人的动作或做法
senses.definition: to copy the way a person speaks, moves, or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 照着别人说话、动作或做事的样子来做
senses.example: Children often imitate the way their parents talk at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们常在饭桌上模仿父母说话的样子。
senses.why: The core of the word is copying, and people are the most obvious thing to copy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心就是「照抄」，而人是最容易被照抄的对象。

senses.title: To follow a style or model
senses.definition: to copy the style of a writer, artist, or product in order to learn from it
senses.definitionCN: 为了学习而照着作家、艺术家或产品的风格去做
senses.example: Many young painters imitate the old masters before finding their own hand.
senses.exampleCN: 许多年轻画家先仿效古典大师，再慢慢找到自己的笔法。
senses.why: Copying moves from the body to the work, and the aim becomes study rather than mockery.
senses.whyCN: 照抄从身体动作延伸到作品上，目的也从逗乐变成了学习。

senses.title: To make a false copy
senses.definition: to make something that looks like an expensive or original product
senses.definitionCN: 做出外形像正品或原作品的东西
senses.example: The market sells bags that imitate famous brands.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场上卖仿冒名牌的包。
senses.why: When the copied thing is a product rather than a gesture, the copying turns into imitation for profit.
senses.whyCN: 当被复制的是商品而不只是动作时，模仿就变成了图利的仿制。

intro.en: Imitate goes back to a Latin verb for copying, and its family has been describing copies for two thousand years.
intro.cn: imitate 源于拉丁语中表示「照抄」的动词，它这一族词两千年来一直在说「复制」这件事。

items.en: Imitari meant to copy or represent something, built on the image of following another's steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imitari 意为「复制、摹拟」，字面意象是跟随着别人的脚步走。

items.en: Imitatio was the noun for a copy or a likeness, and imitator named the person who made it.
items.cn: 名词 imitatio 表示「摹本、相似之物」，imitator 则指做这件事的人。

items.en: Old French took the verb as imiter, keeping the meaning of copying a model.
items.cn: 古法语吸收了这个动词，写作 imiter，仍表示「照着范本做」。

items.en: English borrowed it as imitaten in the sixteenth century, at first in the language of art and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把它借过来，写作 imitaten，最初多用于艺术与修辞的说法里。

items.en: The spelling settled as imitate, and the word widened from art to everyday behaviour and to goods.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 imitate，词义也从艺术扩展到日常行为，乃至商品的仿造。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same imit stem; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of copying.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 imit 词干的词；近义组收其他表示「复制、跟随」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of copying, or a copy that is not the real thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「模仿、仿制品」，指照做的行为或不是真品的东西。

entries.definition: Describing a person or thing that tends to copy others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「模仿的、爱仿效的」，形容人或事物喜欢照搬。

entries.definition: Close and private; it differs from imitate by one consonant and a very different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「亲密的、私人的」，与 imitate 只差一个辅音，意思却完全不同。

entries.definition: To make something exactly the same as another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「复制」，指做出和原件一模一样的东西。

entries.definition: To copy someone's voice or movements, often to make fun of them.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「模仿（声音、举止）」，常带有取笑意味。

entries.definition: To try to equal someone by copying their efforts.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「效法、努力赶超」，指靠模仿去追上别人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the Latin idea of following another's steps to the scenes where imitation happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语「跟着别人的脚步走」的意象，连到模仿真实发生的场景上。

normal.en: I + mitate looks like I meet a mate, and then I copy whatever the mate does.
normal.cn: i 加 mitate 看着像 I meet a mate，遇到同伴之后，同伴做什么我就跟着做什么。

normal.en: imitate and imitation differ only by the noun ending; the verb is what you do, the noun is what comes out.
normal.cn: imitate 与 imitation 只差名词词尾：动词是你做的事，名词是做出来的东西。

normal.en: Children imitate long before they can explain why, so the word describes learning by watching.
normal.cn: 孩子还不会解释为什么要学之前就已经在模仿，所以这个词说的就是「看着学」。

normal.en: A parrot that imitates your voice is not thinking; it is only copying sound.
normal.cn: 鹦鹉模仿你的声音时并没有在想，只是在复制声音。

normal.en: Doctors imitate the sleep of the patient when they follow a ward round: watch, then do.
normal.cn: 医生查房时的学习也是先看后做，正是「模仿」这条路的日常版本。

abstract.en: Imitation is how a culture stores a skill in bodies instead of in books.
abstract.cn: 模仿是文化把技艺存进身体、而不是存进书本的方式。

abstract.en: Every original style starts as an imitation that someone then pushed one step further.
abstract.cn: 每一种独创风格，最初都是一次模仿，只是有人又往前推了一步。

abstract.en: The same act is learning in a child and cheating in a market: the word does not judge, the context does.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作，在小孩身上是学习，在市场上却是欺骗：词本身不评价，语境才评价。

examples.en: He can imitate his teacher accent perfectly.
examples.cn: 他能把老师的口音模仿得惟妙惟肖。

examples.en: Young writers often imitate the authors they love before finding a voice of their own.
examples.cn: 年轻作者常常先模仿自己喜爱的作家，再找到属于自己的声音。

examples.en: Some birds imitate human speech with surprising accuracy.
examples.cn: 有些鸟模仿人说话，准确得令人惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: imit 照着做 + -ate 动词词尾——照着别人的样子做，就是模仿

root: 拉丁语 imitari「复制、摹拟」，由「跟随他人脚步」的意象而来；经古法语 imiter 在十六世纪进入英语，词义从艺术摹仿扩展到日常行为与商品仿造。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: copying a person's actions, following a style in order to learn, and making a false copy of a product.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：模仿他人的动作，为学习而仿效某种风格，以及仿制假冒的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small boy raising a shaving brush to a mirror and copying his father move for move.
core.cn: 核心意象：小男孩对着镜子举起剃须刷，一步一步照着爸爸的样子做。

branches.en: THE BODY: the copy lives in gestures, voices and habits.
branches.cn: 身体线：被复制的是手势、声音与习惯。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: imitating a style is how a beginner learns a craft.
branches.cn: 手艺线：仿效风格是入门者学手艺的路子。

branches.en: THE MARKET: imitation crosses into counterfeiting when money is involved.
branches.cn: 市场线：一旦涉及金钱，模仿就跨到了仿冒。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: imitate, imitation, imitative and imitator all hang on one stem.
branches.cn: 词族线：imitate、imitation、imitative、imitator 都挂在同一个词干上。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: inimitable says no one can copy this, which is a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：inimitable 意为「无人能摹」，反而是句称赞。

intro.en: The affix table shows how the imit stem combines with verb, noun and adjective endings.
intro.cn: 构词表展示 imit 词干如何与动词、名词、形容词词尾组合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms imitari and imitatio sit underneath the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imitari 与 imitatio 是这一整族词的底子。

items.example: She imitates her sister's laugh without noticing.
items.exampleCN: 她没注意自己就在模仿妹妹的笑声。

items.meaning: the act of copying or a copy
items.example: The painting is a fine imitation of an old portrait.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是一幅很不错的古肖像仿作。

items.example: The comedian is a skilled imitator of famous voices.
items.exampleCN: 这位喜剧演员是个模仿名人嗓音的高手。

items.example: Her inimitable style drew a large crowd.
items.exampleCN: 她那无可仿效的风格吸引了大批观众。

items.example: His jump remains unimitated in the league.
items.exampleCN: 他的那一跳在联赛中至今无人仿效。

items.example: Imitative learning shapes how infants pick up language.
items.exampleCN: 模仿式学习决定了婴儿习得语言的方式。

items.example: The boy stood by the window, imitating the conductor.
items.exampleCN: 男孩站在窗边，模仿着乐队指挥。

definition_zh: 校园；校区

scene: 秋天银杏叶落满主路。 Students walked across the campus at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 campus 是「校园」（第 1 个义项：学校的地面与建筑区域）；句意是中午学生们走过校园。

senses.title: The grounds of a school
senses.definition: the land and buildings of a university or college
senses.definitionCN: 大学或学院的土地与建筑
senses.example: Students walked across the campus at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午学生们走过校园。
senses.why: The core image is a field of lawns and buildings for study.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一片草坪与教学楼组成的求学场地。

senses.title: A separate branch of a school
senses.definition: a separate site belonging to the same institution
senses.definitionCN: 同一机构所属的另一处场地
senses.example: The new campus opened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 新校区去年启用。
senses.why: Each separate field of the same school became its own campus.
senses.whyCN: 同一所学校的不同场地，各自成为一个校区。

intro.en: Campus is the Latin word for a field, used first for a college field.
intro.cn: campus 是拉丁语「田野」，最初指学院的场地。

items.en: campus meant a field or open ground.

items.en: American colleges called their grounds a campus.

definition_zh: 祖先；祖宗；（事物的）前身
definition_en: a person from whom one is descended, or an earlier thing from which a later one developed
core_image: 泛黄的族谱上，一代代名字向上延伸
scene: 家里的老相册第一页，是一位从南方迁来的曾祖父。 Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestor 是「祖先」（第 1 个义项：血缘上的先辈）；句意是她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。

derivatives.zh: 名词：前身；先行词，同源于拉丁语「在前」

senses.title: A forebear in the family
senses.definition: a person in one's family line who lived long ago
senses.definitionCN: 家族血脉中生活在很久以前的先辈
senses.example: Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin antecessor, 'one who goes before', so an ancestor is literally a person who walked ahead of us in time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 antecessor「走在前面的人」，所以祖先字面上就是在时间上走在我们前面的人。

senses.title: An earlier form of a thing
senses.definition: an early version or forerunner from which a later thing developed
senses.definitionCN: 后来事物由之发展而来的早期形态或先驱
senses.example: The abacus is an ancestor of the modern calculator.
senses.exampleCN: 算盘是现代计算器的前身。
senses.why: Once the word means 'what came before', it can be applied to machines and ideas, not only to people, which is common in histories of technology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「先前存在的东西」，它就能用于机器与观念，而不只用于人，这在技术史中很常见。

intro.en: Ancestor is a Latin 'one who goes before', filtered through French.
intro.cn: ancestor 是拉丁语「走在前面的人」，经法语传入英语。

items.en: ante meant 'before', in place or in time.
items.cn: ante 意为「在前」，指位置或时间。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go, to yield', the verb of movement.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让」，是表示移动的动词。

items.en: antecessor meant 'a predecessor, one who goes before'.
items.cn: antecessor 意为「前任、走在前头的人」。

items.en: French reshaped the word as ancestre, and English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把词形改造为 ancestre，英语借入。

items.en: English ancestor first meant a family forebear, then extended to forerunners of machines and species.
items.cn: 英语 ancestor 先指家族先辈，后扩展到机器与物种的前身。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ancestry family; the near-meaning group contrasts forebear and descendant.
note.cn: 形近组是 ancestry 词族；近义组对比先辈与后代。

root: 源自拉丁语 antecessor「走在前头的人」，由 ante「在前」与 cedere「走」构成，经古法语 ancestre 进入英语；本指家族先辈，后引申为事物或物种的前身。

sensesIntro.en: The one who goes before can be a family member or an earlier machine.

definition_zh: 汽车（美式非正式说法）；自动的
definition_en: a car, especially in American English, or a setting in which a machine works by itself
core_image: 一辆车自己滑进车位，方向盘没人扶
scene: 朋友在电话里问待会儿怎么过去，说车库里有车。 We took the auto to the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 auto 是「汽车」（第 1 个义项，美式非正式说法）；句意是我们开车去了海边。

senses.title: Car, short form
senses.definition: a car, used mainly in American English as a short form of automobile
senses.definitionCN: 汽车，主要在美式英语中作 automobile 的缩略说法
senses.example: We took the auto to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 我们开车去了海边。
senses.why: The short form appeared when automobiles became common, and American English kept it as a plain everyday word for a car.
senses.whyCN: 汽车普及之后出现了这个缩略形式，美式英语把它保留成日常指车的普通词。

senses.title: Self-working setting
senses.definition: a setting on a machine that lets it work without a person adjusting it
senses.definitionCN: 让机器无需人工调节即可运转的设置
senses.example: Switch the camera to auto and just press the button.
senses.exampleCN: 把相机调到自动模式，然后按快门就行。
senses.why: This use comes from the Greek prefix auto-, 'self': the device handles the adjustment itself, and the word is short for automatic.
senses.whyCN: 这个用法来自希腊语前缀 auto-「自己」：设备自己完成调节，这个词是 automatic 的缩略。

intro.en: Auto is a clipped word standing on a Greek prefix that means self.
intro.cn: auto 是个截短词，站在一个意为「自己」的希腊前缀上。

items.en: autos meant 'self'.
items.cn: autos 意为「自己」。

items.en: The same short form now labels automatic settings.
items.cn: 同一个短形式如今也用来标注自动设置。

definition_zh: 谴责；判刑；定罪；宣布不宜使用
definition_en: to say strongly that something is wrong, or to sentence someone to punishment
core_image: 法官敲下木槌，当庭宣读判决
scene: 邻居们一致指责那家工厂污染了河水。 The whole town condemned the factory for polluting the river.
sceneCN: 这里 condemn 指「谴责」（第 1 个义项：公开表示强烈反对）；句意是全镇人都谴责那家工厂污染河水。

pos.zh: 谴责；判刑；宣布不宜使用

senses.title: Name as wrong
senses.definition: to say in public that something is very wrong
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示某事非常错误
senses.example: The report condemned the use of child labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告谴责使用童工的行为。
senses.why: A public voice turns private dislike into a shared judgement.
senses.whyCN: 公开的声音把私人的反感变成共同的评判。

senses.title: Give a punishment
senses.definition: to order a legal punishment for someone
senses.definitionCN: 依法对某人作出惩罚判决
senses.example: The court condemned him to life in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处他终身监禁。
senses.why: The court speaks with the weight of the whole community behind it.
senses.whyCN: 法庭说话时，背后是整个共同体的分量。

senses.title: Declare unsafe
senses.definition: to officially state that a building or object cannot be used
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某建筑或物品不能继续使用
senses.example: Inspectors condemned the old school building.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员宣布这栋旧校舍不宜使用。
senses.why: A thing judged unfit is given a sentence just as a person is.
senses.whyCN: 被判定不合格的东西，也像人一样被判了刑。

intro.en: Condemn comes from Latin condemnare, to sentence or blame, built from com-, fully, and damnare, to harm or find guilty.
intro.cn: condemn 来自拉丁语 condemnare，意为判罪或指责，由 com-（彻底）与 damnare（损害、定罪）构成。

items.en: Damnare meant to find someone guilty and set a penalty.
items.cn: damnare 意为判定某人有罪并定下惩罚。

items.en: Condemnare added com- to make the judgement complete.
items.cn: condemnare 加上 com-，表示判决彻底成立。

items.en: Old French condemner carried the legal sense into common use.
items.cn: 古法语 condemner 把这个法律含义带入日常用法。

items.en: English condemn first meant to sentence a person in court.
items.cn: 英语 condemn 最初指在法庭上给人判刑。

items.en: It now also means to state strong moral disapproval in public.
items.cn: 如今它也指在公开场合表达强烈的道德反对。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like condemn, and the meaning group names other ways of blaming or punishing.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 condemn 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他指责或惩罚的说法。

entries.definition: to accept wrong behaviour without blame
to make something shorter or denser
to argue for something or compete
to criticize someone or something strongly in public
to point out faults in something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a court ruling, then move to a public protest and to a building marked unsafe.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从法庭判决开始，再走到公开抗议与被标记为危险的建筑。

normal.en: Con- means fully and damn- means to find guilty, so to condemn is to find fully guilty.
normal.cn: con- 表示彻底，damn- 表示定罪，所以 condemn 就是把罪名彻底定下。

normal.en: A judge condemns with a hammer, and a crowd condemns with a shout.
normal.cn: 法官用木槌定罪，人群用喊声谴责。

normal.en: Condemn and damn share the same core, which is why the word feels so heavy.
normal.cn: condemn 与 damn 共享同一个核心，所以这个词听起来很重。

normal.en: A condemned building is a building that has been sentenced.
normal.cn: 一栋被判定的建筑，就是一栋被宣判的建筑。

normal.en: Strong words condemn, and strong walls condemn too.
normal.cn: 强烈的话语在谴责，坚固的墙也可能被判为不能用。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden hammer falling on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一把木槌落在桌面上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of raised hands in a meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上举起的一排手。

abstract.en: Picture a red sign nailed to a broken door.
abstract.cn: 想象一块红色告示钉在破损的门上。

examples.en: World leaders condemned the attack on the hospital.
examples.cn: 各国领导人谴责了针对医院的袭击。

examples.en: He was condemned to five years in prison.
examples.cn: 他被判处五年监禁。

examples.en: Engineers condemned the bridge after the flood.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 condemn 记成 con（彻底）加 demn（定罪）：把罪名彻底定下来，就是谴责与判刑。

root: 源自拉丁语 condemnare（com 彻底 + damnare 定罪），本义是判定有罪，后引申为公开谴责与宣布废弃。

sensesIntro.en: From a court sentence, to a public moral judgement, and finally to a building declared unfit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法庭判决，到公开的道德评判，最后到被宣布不能使用的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer falls and a whole crowd agrees with the verdict.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，全场人都认同这个判决。

branches.en: Condemnation by words needs an audience to become powerful.
branches.cn: 用言语谴责，需要听众才能产生力量。

branches.en: The legal sense gives the word its official weight.
branches.cn: 法律义项赋予这个词官方的分量。

branches.en: Buildings and objects can receive the same verdict.
branches.cn: 建筑和物品也会收到同样的判决。

branches.en: Both blame and punish by naming the act as wrong.
branches.cn: 谴责与判刑都先把行为认定为错误。

branches.en: A person and a place can both be sentenced out of use.
branches.cn: 人与地方都可能被判为不能再使用。

intro.en: Condemn is built on Latin com-, fully, plus damnare, to find guilty.

definition_en: to keep something under control, or the raised stone edge of a road

scene: 骑手拉紧缰绳，让跑得太快的马慢下来。 The city hopes to curb the rise in traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 curb 指「抑制、控制」（第 1 个义项：让某事不再增长或加剧）；句意是这座城市希望抑制交通量的增长。

senses.title: Hold something back
senses.definition: to keep something from growing or getting worse
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某事增长或恶化
senses.example: New rules curb the use of plastic bags.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定限制塑料袋的使用。
senses.why: A strong force needs a bit to hold it.
senses.whyCN: 强大的力量需要一点东西勒住。

senses.definition: the raised stone edge along a road
senses.definitionCN: 路边凸起的石边
senses.example: She parked the car at the curb.
senses.exampleCN: 她把车停在路边。
senses.why: A low stone line keeps wheels off the grass.
senses.whyCN: 一条矮石线，把车轮挡在草外。

senses.title: A check or limit
senses.definition: a limit placed on something
senses.definitionCN: 加在某事上的限制
senses.example: The government put a curb on spending.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对开支设了限制。
senses.why: A curb is a line you are not meant to cross.
senses.whyCN: 路缘是一条不该越过的线。

intro.en: Curb comes from Old French courbe, curved, from Latin curvus, bent; a curb bit was a curved piece of metal for a horse.
intro.cn: curb 源自古法语 courbe（弯曲之物），更早出自拉丁语 curvus（弯的）；勒马的马衔就是一块弯金属。

items.en: Curvus meant bent or curved.
items.cn: curvus 意为弯曲的。

items.en: Courbe named something curved.
items.cn: courbe 指弯曲之物。

items.en: Curb first meant a curved bit for a horse.
items.cn: curb 最初指勒马的弯形马衔。

items.en: It came to mean a check or restraint.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示制止与约束。

items.en: It also named the stone edge of a street.
items.cn: 它也指街道边凸起的石缘。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- opening, and the meaning group names other ways of holding something back.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 开头，近义组列出其他拉住某物的说法。

entries.definition: a solid with six square faces
a curved piece of hair
to make a sick person well
to hold someone back from acting
entries.definitionCN: 拉住某人使其不作某事

entries.definition: to keep something below a level
entries.definitionCN: 使某事不超过某一水平

entries.definition: the outer line of a surface

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pulled rein and end with a low stone line beside a road.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被拉紧的缰绳开始，落到路边一条矮石线。

normal.en: A curb bit sits in a horse's mouth and asks it to slow.
normal.cn: 马衔放在马嘴里，请它慢下来。

normal.en: To curb a thing is to put a bit on it.
normal.cn: curb 一件事，就是给它套上嚼子。

normal.en: Curb the temper before it becomes a shout.
normal.cn: 在脾气变成喊声前先勒住它。

normal.en: The curb keeps cars off the grass.
normal.cn: 路缘把车挡在草地外。

normal.en: Every fast thing needs a small edge to stop it.
normal.cn: 每个太快的东西，都需要一道小边来挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a horse slowing as the reins go tight.
abstract.cn: 想象缰绳一紧，马就慢下来。

abstract.en: Picture a shoe stepping off a stone edge into the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋从石边踩下马路。

abstract.en: Picture a red line on a chart flattening out.
abstract.cn: 想象图上一根红线渐渐变平。

examples.en: The new tax is meant to curb waste.
examples.cn: 这项新税意在抑制浪费。

examples.en: He curbed his anger and spoke softly.
examples.cn: 他压住怒火，轻声说话。

examples.en: A bicycle lay against the curb.
examples.cn: 一辆自行车靠在路缘上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curb 记成「勒住」：马的弯曲嚼子勒住速度，就是抑制。

root: 源自古法语 courbe（弯曲之物），更早出自拉丁语 curvus（弯的）；本义是勒马的弯曲嚼子，后引申为约束与路缘。

sensesIntro.en: From pulling a horse back, to limiting a force, to a stone edge beside the road.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把马勒住，到限制一股力量，再到路边的石缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling a rein to slow a horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拉紧缰绳让马慢下来。

branches.en: A check keeps a strong force from running away.
branches.cn: 约束让强大的力量不至于失控。

branches.en: The stone edge is a curb for wheels.
branches.cn: 石缘是给车轮设的路缘。

branches.en: A limit is a line drawn and kept.
branches.cn: 限制是一条画下并守住的线。

branches.en: To curb and to set a curb are the same act.
branches.cn: 抑制与设限是同一个动作。

branches.en: A road edge shows how a limit looks in stone.
branches.cn: 路缘把限制的样子用石头做出来。

intro.en: Curb forms words for restraining, for the horse bit, and for the stone edge of a street.
intro.cn: curb 组成一族词，关于抑制、马衔与街道石缘。

latinIntro.en: The Latin curvus, bent, is the root behind curb and its compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 curvus（弯的）是 curb 及其合成词背后的根。

definition_zh: 辅助的，备用的；辅助人员；助动词
definition_en: giving extra help or support, a person or thing that helps, or a verb used with a main verb
core_image: 主发动机旁边还有一台小机器，随时准备接手
scene: 医院停电的那一秒，备用电源自己接了上来。 The auxiliary generator started at once.
sceneCN: 这里 auxiliary 是「备用的、辅助的」（第 1 个义项：提供额外支持）；句意是备用发电机立刻启动了。

derivatives.zh: 名词：辅助人员；助动词（复数）

senses.title: Giving extra support
senses.definition: giving additional help or serving as a reserve
senses.definitionCN: 提供额外帮助或作为后备的
senses.example: The auxiliary generator started at once.
senses.exampleCN: 备用发电机立刻启动了。
senses.why: The Latin base auxilium means help, so the adjective marks whatever stands beside the main thing and helps when needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 auxilium 意为「帮助」，所以这个形容词标记的是站在主体旁边、需要时出手帮忙的东西。

senses.title: Helper or support worker
senses.definition: a person or group that gives support to a main body
senses.definitionCN: 为主要机构提供支持的人或队伍
senses.example: The hospital hired more auxiliary staff.
senses.exampleCN: 医院雇用了更多辅助人员。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun for the people who provide the help, especially in hospitals, armies and offices.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成可数名词，指提供帮助的那些人，在医院、军队与机关里尤其常见。

senses.title: Helping verb
senses.definition: a verb such as be, have or will that helps form another verb's tense or voice
senses.definitionCN: be、have、will 这类帮助构成另一个动词时态或语态的动词
senses.example: In this sentence, will is an auxiliary.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，will 是助动词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the same idea: the helping verb carries tense or voice while the main verb carries the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了同一个思路：助动词承担时态或语态，主要动词承担词义。

intro.en: Auxiliary comes from a Latin word for help.
intro.cn: auxiliary 来自拉丁语中表示「帮助」的词。

items.en: auxilium meant 'help or support'.
items.cn: auxilium 意为「帮助、支援」。

items.en: auxiliarius meant 'giving help'.
items.cn: auxiliarius 意为「提供帮助的」。

items.en: auxilia named supporting troops.
items.cn: auxilia 指辅助部队。

items.en: French auxiliaire carried both the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 法语 auxiliaire 兼有形容词与名词用法。

items.en: English added the grammar sense of a helping verb.
items.cn: 英语又加上了「助动词」这一语法义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auxili- stem; the near-meaning group gives words for support and reserve.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auxili- 词干；近义组是表示支持与后备的词。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: awg-ZIL-yuh-ree.

normal.en: Auxiliary verb is the phrase to remember for grammar.

normal.en: The plural is auxiliaries, and it often means support staff.

normal.en: Auxiliary power is the electricity kept for emergencies.

normal.en: Do not confuse it with auxiliary's look-alike auxin, a plant hormone.
normal.cn: 不要与形近词 auxin 混淆，那是植物生长素。

abstract.en: See a small engine switch on beside a big one.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小发动机在大发动机旁边启动。

abstract.en: See a second key already in the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象第二把钥匙已经插在锁里。

abstract.en: See a helping hand steady a ladder from below.

sensesIntro.cn: 帮助可以是一台机器、一个人，也可以是一个动词。
