definition_zh: 雷；雷声；轰隆声；怒吼
definition_en: the loud noise that follows lightning in a storm, or any very loud rolling sound
core_image: 乌云压顶，一道白光之后整片天空轰隆隆地滚过
scene: 夏夜的雨来得急,雷声在孩子头顶滚过,他一下子钻进被子里。 The thunder rolled across the valley and the child hid under the blanket.
sceneCN: 这里 thunder 是「雷声」（第 1 个义项：雷雨中紧随闪电的巨大声响）；句意为雷声滚过山谷，孩子躲进了被子里。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「雷鸣般的；轰响的」
由 thunder 与 storm 复合，义为「雷暴」
由 thunder 与 bolt 复合，义为「霹雳；雷电」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「有雷的；闷热欲雷的」

senses.title: The noise after lightning
senses.definition: the loud rolling noise heard after a flash of lightning during a storm
senses.definitionCN: 雷雨中闪电之后听到的巨大滚响
senses.example: A clap of thunder woke the whole house.
senses.exampleCN: 一声炸雷惊醒了整幢房子。
senses.why: Thor, the hammer-wielding god of storms, hides in the first syllable of this word.
senses.whyCN: 手持锤子的雷神托尔（Thor）就藏在这个词的第一个音节里。

senses.title: Any loud rolling sound
senses.definition: a very loud, deep and continuing noise made by traffic, water, applause or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 车辆、水流、掌声或人群发出的响亮而低沉的连续声响
senses.example: The thunder of the waterfall could be heard a mile away.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布的轰鸣声一英里外就能听到。
senses.why: Any sound as deep and continuous as a storm borrows the storm’s name.
senses.whyCN: 凡是像风暴那样低沉而持续的声音，都可以借用风暴的名字。

senses.title: To make a loud rolling noise
senses.definition: to make a loud deep noise, or for the sky to sound with thunder
senses.definitionCN: 发出响亮低沉的声响，或指天上打雷
senses.example: The trucks thundered past on the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在老桥上一路轰隆而过。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical roar: heavy things moving with a rolling noise.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留实体的轰鸣：沉重之物带着滚动之声前进。

senses.title: To shout angrily
senses.definition: to speak very loudly and angrily, often of a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 大声而愤怒地说话，多指有权威的人
senses.example: The coach thundered at the players to get back in line.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对球员怒吼，叫他们排好队。
senses.why: A human voice raised to storm volume takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人声抬到风暴的音量，就用同一个词。

intro.en: Thunder is named after Thor, the Germanic god of storms, and the word has kept his hammer in its sound.
intro.cn: thunder 取自日耳曼雷神 Thor 之名，读音里还留着那把锤子的分量。

items.en: The common Germanic word for the storm god was Thunraz, borrowed as Thor in Norse and Thunor in Old English.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中雷神之名为 Thunraz，北欧语作 Thor，古英语作 Thunor。

items.en: Old English þunor was both the god and the noise he was thought to make, so the natural sound and the god shared one name.
items.cn: 古英语 þunor 既是神，也是人们认为神发出的响声，自然之声与神共用一个名字。

items.en: When the speaker d moved into the word, the spelling thunder fixed the modern form and the god faded from it.
items.cn: 插入了 d 音之后，拼写 thunder 固定下来，神的身影也跟着隐去。

items.en: Modern English extends thunder to engines, crowds and waterfalls, and the verb to angry speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到引擎、人群与瀑布，动词则扩用于愤怒的说话。

items.en: Idioms such as steal someone’s thunder still remember a storm that can be taken away.
items.cn: steal someone’s thunder 一类习语，仍记得那场可以被夺走的风暴。

note.en: The first group gathers the thunder family and near spellings; the second compares loud natural sounds.
note.cn: 第一组收 thunder 词族与形近词；第二组比较自然界的大声响。

entries.definition: The adjective, as in thunderous applause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如「雷鸣般的掌声」

entries.definition: A storm with thunder and lightning.
A flash of lightning with a crash, and a sudden shock.
Beneath something; it hides inside thunder but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面（藏在 thunder 之中，词源不同）

entries.definition: The flash of electricity in a storm; it comes before the thunder.
entries.definitionCN: 闪电（雷雨中的电光，先于雷声）

entries.definition: A low continuous sound, often further away and weaker than thunder.
A very loud deep sound made by a lion, crowd, engine or sea.
entries.definitionCN: 咆哮；轰鸣（多由狮、人群、引擎或海发出）

entries.definition: A short deep explosive sound, like a drum.
entries.definitionCN: 低沉的爆响（短促，如鼓声）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the god Thor, the silent-looking d and the storms the word names.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自雷神 Thor、看起来「多出来」的 d，以及它命名的各种风暴。

normal.en: Thor is the thunder god, and his name is the first four letters.
normal.cn: Thor 是雷神，他的名字就是这个词的前四个字母。

normal.en: The d was added by speakers, so thunder sounds nothing like its spelling suggests.
normal.cn: 这个 d 是口语里后加的，读音与拼写差得很远。

normal.en: Thunder follows lightning; the light comes first and the sound arrives later.
normal.cn: thunder 跟在 lightning 之后：先见光，后闻声。

normal.en: Thunderous applause has nothing to do with storms but the volume.
normal.cn: 雷鸣般的掌声与风暴无关，只是音量相似。

normal.en: Steal someone’s thunder means to take the credit before they can speak.
normal.cn: steal someone’s thunder 意为抢在别人开口前抢走功劳。

abstract.en: Picture a whole sky rolling over like a heavy barrel down a stone road.
abstract.cn: 想象整片天空像一只重桶在石路上滚过。

abstract.en: The same word names the weather, applause and an angry voice.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名天气，也命名掌声与怒声。

abstract.en: Thunder is the sound of something enormous happening out of sight.
abstract.cn: thunder 是某件巨大之事在视野之外发生时的响动。

examples.en: Thunder rolled over the hills all evening.
examples.cn: 整个傍晚雷声都在山间滚动。

examples.en: The audience gave the singer thunderous applause.
examples.cn: 观众给歌手送上了雷鸣般的掌声。

examples.en: The waves thundered against the harbour wall.
examples.cn: 海浪轰隆隆地拍打着港口墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「散得」——满天闷响一时散得干干净净 → thunder 雷声

root: 古英语 þunor，源自日耳曼雷神之名 Thunraz（北欧语 Thor），一词兼指雷神与其轰鸣；中古英语插入 d 音定型为 thunder，后引申为一切轰响与怒吼。

sensesIntro.en: Thunder begins as the voice of the storm god and spreads to every deep, rolling noise, from engines to angry coaches.
sensesIntro.cn: thunder 起初是雷神的声音，后来扩散到一切低沉滚动的巨响，从引擎到怒吼的教练。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sky rolling over like a barrel on stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：整片天空像桶滚石路一般碾压而过。

branches.en: The weather: a storm’s deep voice.
branches.cn: 天气线：风暴的低沉嗓音。

branches.en: The world: waterfalls, lorries and applause.
branches.cn: 世界线：瀑布、卡车与掌声。

branches.en: The action: a sky or engine that thunders.
branches.cn: 动作线：天空或引擎在轰响。

branches.en: The voice: authority raised into a roar.
branches.cn: 人声线：权威抬高成咆哮。

branches.en: Storm and machinery borrow each other’s volume.
branches.cn: 风暴与机械互相借用彼此的音量。

intro.en: Thunder takes -ous and -y, and compounds with storm and bolt.
intro.cn: thunder 可加 -ous、-y，并与 storm、bolt 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, though -ous and -y are borrowed endings that English applies freely.
latinIntro.cn: 词干为日耳曼语，-ous 与 -y 是英语借入后自由使用的后缀。

items.meaning: a lightning flash with a crash

definition_zh: 泵；抽水机；用泵抽送；打气；投入（资金）；上下抽动
definition_en: a machine that forces liquid or gas through a pipe; to move liquid or gas with such a machine; to fill something with air; to pour money into something; to move a handle or a limb up and down
core_image: 院子里一台旧铁泵，手柄一压一抬，清澈的水就顺着铁嘴流进木桶
scene: 院子里那台旧铁家伙生了锈，可手柄压下去再抬起来，水还是照样从铁嘴里涌出来。 The old pump in the yard still lifts water from the well.
sceneCN: 这里 pump 是「泵、抽水机」（第 1 个义项：靠往复运动把水或气强制送出的机器）；句意为院子里那台旧泵仍能把井水抽上来。图中可辨识物件：铸铁泵体、手柄、木桶。

pos.zh: 用泵抽送；打气；投入；上下抽动

derivatives.zh: pump 加表人或表工具的后缀 -er，指操作泵的人，也指消防泵车
pump 与 house 复合，指安放泵的泵房
pump 加 -ing 构成的动名词，指抽送这一动作

senses.title: A machine that forces liquid or gas along
senses.definition: a machine that pushes liquid or gas through a pipe or into a container by pressure or suction
senses.definitionCN: 靠压力或吸力把液体、气体压过管道或压进容器的机器
senses.example: The village well has an iron pump beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 村口那口井旁边有一台铁泵。
senses.why: The word first named a simple wooden device worked by hand in mines and ships, and the machine kept the name even after steam and electricity replaced the handle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指矿井与船上那种靠手压的木制装置，后来即便蒸汽与电力取代了手柄，机器仍旧叫这个名字。

senses.title: To move liquid or gas with such a machine
senses.definition: to make liquid or gas flow by means of a pump or by a similar pushing and sucking motion
senses.definitionCN: 借助泵或类似的推吸动作使液体、气体流动
senses.example: They pumped the flooded cellar dry overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一夜之间把灌水的地窖抽干了。
senses.why: Once the tool has a name, the work it performs takes the same word as a verb, so pumping is simply the machine's action applied to a place.
senses.whyCN: 工具一旦有了名字，它干的活就用同一个词作动词，所以 pumping 不过是把机器的动作施加到某个地方。

senses.title: To fill something with air
senses.definition: to force air into a tyre, a ball or a mattress until it is firm
senses.definitionCN: 把空气压进轮胎、球或床垫，直到它们鼓起来
senses.example: He pumped up the back tyre before the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他给后胎打了气。
senses.why: Air is a gas, so the same verb that moves water through a pipe also pushes air into a closed rubber space until it tightens.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种气体，于是原本把水送过管道的动词，也被用来把空气压进封闭的橡胶空间，直到它绷紧。

senses.title: To pour money or resources into something
senses.definition: to put large amounts of money, energy or information into something in a steady stream
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、精力或信息以持续不断的方式大量投入某事
senses.example: The city has pumped millions into the new line.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市已为新线路投入了数百万资金。
senses.why: Money is made to flow like water through a pipe, so the image of forcing a fluid steadily in one direction is applied to funding.
senses.whyCN: 钱被安排得像水一样从管子里流，于是「把流体稳定压向一方」的形象被搬用到资金上。

senses.title: To move up and down or in and out repeatedly
senses.definition: to move a handle, a limb or a part of the body quickly up and down or in and out
senses.definitionCN: 把手柄、肢体或身体某部分快速地上下来回或进出移动
senses.example: His heart pumped hard after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途爬坡之后，他的心脏剧烈跳动。
senses.why: The handle of an old pump must be worked up and down, and that repeated motion became a sense of its own, applied to fists, pedals and a beating heart.
senses.whyCN: 旧泵的手柄必须一上一下地压，这个反复的动作本身也成了一个义项，被用到拳头、踏板和跳动的心脏上。

intro.en: Pump appears in late Middle English, probably borrowed from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pompe; the further origin is uncertain and no reliable Latin source is recorded, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pump 出现于中古英语后期，一般认为借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 pompe；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁语源头，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: The word is first recorded in English in the fifteenth century as pumpe, naming a device for lifting water out of a ship or a mine.
items.cn: 这个词十五世纪以 pumpe 的形式首次见于英语，指把水从船上或矿井里提上来的装置。

items.en: It is generally thought to be borrowed from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German pompe, the word used by the sailors and miners who worked such devices.
items.cn: 一般认为它借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 pompe，那是操作这类装置的水手与矿工所用的词。

items.en: Beyond that point the trail is uncertain; some scholars link the form to a sucking or thumping sound, but no source is agreed.
items.cn: 再往前追溯就不确定了；有学者把这个形式与吸吮或撞击的声音联系起来，但没有公认的源头。

items.en: By the seventeenth century pump covers ship pumps, mine pumps and the verb, and the handle-driven machine spreads to wells and gardens.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，pump 已涵盖船泵、矿泵及相应动词，这种手柄驱动的机器也推广到水井与园圃。

items.en: Modern English pumps petrol, air and money, and the up-and-down motion survives in phrases such as pump iron and pump a fist.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pump 输送汽油、空气和金钱，而上下抽动的动作仍留在 pump iron、pump a fist 这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ from pump by a single consonant; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving liquid, air or money in a steady flow.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pump 只差一个辅音的词；近义组收其他表示「让液体、空气或钱持续流动」的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 轻轻的一撞，或表面上隆起的一块。

normalIntro.en: The word names a hand-worked device for lifting water, and every later sense keeps the idea of forcing something to move in one direction.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本指靠手操作的提水装置，后来每个义项都保留着「把东西强制推向一个方向」的意思。

normal.en: Pump entered English in the fifteenth century, probably from Dutch or Low German pompe, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
normal.cn: pump 十五世纪进入英语，一般认为来自荷兰语或低地德语的 pompe，更早的源头不确定。

normal.en: Pumper adds -er: the person who works the pump, or the fire engine that carries one.
normal.cn: pumper 加 -er：操作泵的人，或载着泵的消防车。

normal.en: Pump up works the same way as a bicycle pump: air goes in and the rubber tightens.
normal.cn: pump up 的作用就像打气筒：空气进去，橡胶绷紧。

normal.en: Pump money into a project borrows the pipe: the flow is steady and aimed at one place.
normal.cn: pump money into 借用了管子的形象：流量稳定，而且只朝一个地方。

normal.en: Pump iron is not about water at all; it keeps only the up-and-down motion of the handle.
normal.cn: pump iron 与水和气都无关，它只保留了手柄一上一下的动作。

abstract.en: A pump is a promise that what is below can be brought up, if someone keeps working the handle.
abstract.cn: 泵是一种承诺：只要有人持续压动手柄，下面的东西就能被提上来。

abstract.en: The same verb serves water, air and money because all three can be made to flow in one direction.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词同时服务水、空气和钱，因为这三样都能被逼着朝一个方向流动。

abstract.en: Repetition is the whole machine: one stroke does little, ten thousand strokes empty a flooded room.
abstract.cn: 重复就是整台机器：一次行程微不足道，上万次就能抽干一间灌水的屋子。

examples.en: The farmers pump water from the river into the fields.
examples.cn: 农民把河水抽到田里。

examples.en: She pumped up her bike tyres before leaving.
examples.cn: 出发前她给自行车轮胎打了气。

examples.en: Investors pumped more money into the project last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天投资者向这个项目投入了更多资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「啪噗」——手柄一压，管口啪噗一声，水就上来了，记住 pump 是泵。

root: 中古英语后期 pumpe，一般认为借自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 pompe（提水装置），更早来源不确定，无可靠拉丁同族词；核心是「靠反复推压把流体送出去」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand-worked device that pushes fluid one way; the senses divide into the machine, the act of moving liquid, filling with air, pouring money in, and the up-and-down stroke itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「靠人力把流体朝一个方向推出去的装置」；义项由此分为机器本身、抽送液体、充气、投入资金，以及那个上下压动的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron pump in a yard, its handle pressed down and lifted, clear water running into a wooden bucket.
core.cn: 核心意象：院子里一台铁泵，手柄压下又抬起，清水流进木桶。

branches.cn: 村口井边生锈的铁家伙

branches.en: a cellar floor drying after a flood
branches.cn: 洪水退后慢慢变干的地窖地面

branches.en: a tyre growing firm under the nozzle
branches.cn: 在气嘴下渐渐绷紧的轮胎

branches.en: money arriving in a steady line
branches.cn: 一笔接一笔不断到来的资金

branches.en: a fist driving the air again and again
branches.cn: 一次次挥向空中的拳头

intro.en: The word is held together by a Middle English noun of uncertain borrowing, its Dutch or Low German ancestor, and the English endings and compounds that grew from it.
intro.cn: 这个词由来源不确定的中古英语名词、它在荷兰语或低地德语中的祖先，以及由它长出的英语后缀与复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 咀嚼；嚼碎；反复琢磨
definition_en: to crush food with the teeth before swallowing, or to think about something again and again
core_image: 闭着嘴慢慢咀嚼的人
scene: 食堂里人声嘈杂，盘子碰得叮当响。 He chewed each mouthful slowly and said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 chew 指「咀嚼」（第 1 个义项：用牙齿反复嚼碎食物）；句意是他每一口都慢慢咀嚼，什么也没说。

senses.title: To crush food with the teeth
senses.definition: to break food into small pieces with the teeth before swallowing
senses.definitionCN: 吞咽之前用牙齿把食物弄碎
senses.example: Chew your food before you swallow it.
senses.exampleCN: 吞下去之前先把食物嚼碎。
senses.why: The Old English verb named the work of the jaws, and that physical sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词本指颌部的动作，这一身体义从未改变。

senses.title: To think something over
senses.definition: to consider an idea or a problem slowly and repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而反复地思考某个想法或问题
senses.example: He chewed over the offer for a whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个提议反复琢磨了整整一周。
senses.why: Turning food in the mouth became a picture for turning an idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里翻动食物，成了脑中翻动想法的比喻。

intro.en: Chew is an old English verb that has kept its bodily meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: chew 是一个古英语动词，一千年间一直保留着身体动作的含义。

items.en: Kewwan meant to chew or to crush with the teeth.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kewwan 意为咀嚼或用牙弄碎。

items.en: Ceowan named the action of the jaws on food.
items.cn: 古英语 ceowan 指颌部对食物的动作。

items.en: Chewen kept the plain food sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 chewen 保留单纯的食物义。

items.en: The phrase chew over stretched the action to thinking.
items.cn: chew over 这一说法把动作延伸到思考。

items.en: Chewy and chewing gum joined the family later.
items.cn: chewy 与 chewing gum 后来加入这个词族。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists ways of biting food.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出咬食物的各种方式。

a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

to cut into something with the teeth

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw relatives, the chew over idiom and the chewy adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌部同源词、chew over 习语以及形容词 chewy。

normal.en: Chew and cheek come from the same jaw area: one is the action, the other the flesh.
normal.cn: chew 与 cheek 都出自颌部：一个是动作，一个是皮肉。

normal.en: Chew over means to turn a problem in the mind as if it were food.
normal.cn: chew over 意为把问题当食物一样在脑子里翻来覆去。

normal.en: Chewy describes meat or candy that resists the teeth.
normal.cn: chewy 形容需要用牙使劲的肉或糖。

normal.en: The past tense is simply chewed, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: 过去式就是 chewed，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Chewing gum keeps the mouth busy without any food.
normal.cn: chewing gum 让嘴一直动着，却不是在吃东西。

abstract.en: Picture a man eating slowly while the table talks around him.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人慢慢吃着，桌边的人都在说话。

abstract.en: Picture a pen top flattened by nervous teeth.
abstract.cn: 想象笔帽被紧张的牙咬扁。

abstract.en: Picture a cow's jaw moving in a steady circle.
abstract.cn: 想象牛的下颌一圈圈不停地动。

examples.en: The meat was too tough to chew.
examples.cn: 这肉太硬，嚼不动。

examples.en: She chewed her sandwich while reading the report.
examples.cn: 她一边嚼三明治一边看报告。

examples.en: Give him time to chew over the plan.
examples.cn: 给他时间反复考虑这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: chew 与 cheek 同源：动的是下巴和脸颊，嚼的是嘴里的东西。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kewwan（咀嚼），古英语作 ceowan，中古英语作 chewen，身体义沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: The teeth crushing food gives the physical sense, and the same turning motion gives the mental sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 牙齿弄碎食物给出身体义，而同样的翻动动作给出心理义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: teeth working slowly on a mouthful of food.
core.cn: 核心意象：牙齿慢慢对付一口食物。

branches.en: Food is crushed before it is swallowed.
branches.cn: 食物在吞下之前被嚼碎。

branches.en: An idea is turned over the same way.
branches.cn: 一个想法也以同样方式被反复翻动。

branches.en: Chewy food resists the teeth for a while.
branches.cn: 有嚼劲的食物会让牙齿多费些力。

branches.en: Both senses share a slow repeated motion.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享缓慢重复的动作。

branches.en: Chew over keeps the food picture in the mind.
branches.cn: chew over 把食物的画面留在脑中。

intro.en: Chew has a small family built from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: chew 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, not Latin, so the oldest layers are English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，最古老的层次是英语与日耳曼语。
